question: When should you make sure your passengers have fastened their seat belts?
options: a:Before you start the engine.,b:Only when it is raining or snowing.,c:Only if the vehicle will be driven long distances.,d:Only after a police officer instructs you to do so.
note: Seat belts are the best protection in a crash. Ensure you and your passengers have fastened seat belts before starting the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs represent?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:A suggested driving speed for heavy traffic only.,c:A recommended safe speed in all conditions.,d:Speeds enforceable only at night.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (or sometimes minimum) legal speed in ideal conditions. Drivers must slow down when conditions require.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what precaution should you take?
options: a:Honk to warn anyone who might step out.,b:Be prepared for people or vehicles to unexpectedly enter your lane and keep a safe space.,c:Assume parked vehicles will remain stationary.,d:Drive close to parked cars to discourage doors opening.
note: Leave space between your vehicle and parked cars. Watch for people exiting vehicles or cars pulling out unexpectedly.

question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren approaches, must drivers pull to the right edge and wait?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: When approached by an authorized emergency vehicle, you must pull to the right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, which documents must you be prepared to show?
options: a:Proof of registration, your license, and proof of insurance.,b:Only your license.,c:Only proof of insurance.,d:Only proof of registration.
note: When stopped, a driver must produce their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance upon request.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk — True or False?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must come to a complete stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on the driver's side when there are no traffic signals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is part of correct passing procedure?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,c:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,d:All of the above
note: When passing, signal well in advance, check mirrors and blind spot, and return to your lane only when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes on a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and no passing is allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and generally discourage or prohibit lane changes.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should a small-vehicle driver be prepared for?
options: a:Loud music from the truck.,b:Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.,c:Less road noise.,d:Reduced engine power.
note: Large vehicles can create wind gusts that affect smaller vehicles. Be ready to correct steering when passing or being passed by large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, what important action must you take?
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.,d:Stop and back up slightly.
note: Before making a left turn, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and proceed only when the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection with a green light but heavy oncoming traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear before turning.,b:Use the next intersection to turn instead.,c:Turn quickly and hope oncoming traffic yields.,d:Stop in the middle of the intersection and wave oncoming traffic through.
note: If turning left, you may enter the intersection to position for the turn on a green light, but wait there until oncoming traffic clears before completing the turn.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the dividing line between lanes is which type?
options: a:Broken white line,b:Solid yellow line,c:Double solid yellow
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, how should you react?
options: a:Pull over to the right and stop.,b:Stop where you are.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle by safely pulling over to the right and stopping. In heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of its way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: The posted maximum speed limit is always the safest speed to drive.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on highways,d:Only during daylight
note: The posted limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions. You must slow for poor visibility, slippery roads, or other unsafe conditions.

question: A curb painted which color indicates only short parking stops are allowed?
options: a:Blue,b:White,c:Yellow
note: Painted curbs show parking rules. A white curb indicates only brief stops are permitted (for example, to pick up or drop off passengers).

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, which is true?
options: a:Require a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles do.,b:Require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles do.,c:Require less time to pass on a downgrade than smaller vehicles do.
note: Because of their size and weight, large trucks need greater stopping distances than smaller vehicles.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do next?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.,c:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
note: After a bus stops for children, exercise caution and watch for kids walking along the road before proceeding.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Remove your foot from the accelerator and gradually steer back onto the roadway when safe.,b:Stop quickly.,c:Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.
note: Do not panic; lift off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, slow down, and carefully ease back onto the pavement when it is safe.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Towards the right edge of the road ahead.,b:Directly into the oncoming headlights.,c:At the center of the road.
note: If another driver fails to dim high beams, keep your eyes on the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes to avoid temporary blindness from glare.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow signal mean?
options: a:Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.,c:Is never used as a traffic signal.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turning interval is ending and has the same cautionary meaning as a circular yellow light.

question: When changing lanes, what should you not rely on exclusively?
options: a:Relying only on your mirrors.,b:Signaling after you begin moving into the lane.,c:Signaling 500 feet before a lane change in residential areas.
note: Don’t rely solely on mirrors—always check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder before changing lanes, and signal appropriately before moving.

question: Do you need to allow as much following distance when following a motorcycle as when following a car?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcyclists can stop more quickly but are more vulnerable; you should allow at least three to four seconds following distance for safety.

question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That you are changing lanes.,c:That your emergency brake is on.,d:That you are making a right turn.
note: Brake lights signal to following drivers that you are slowing down or stopping; they must be kept in working order.

question: When stopped on an incline, you should allow:
options: a:Extra space in front of your vehicle to prevent collisions if the vehicle ahead rolls back,b:Less space than usual because gravity holds cars in place,c:No extra space
note: On an uphill stop leave additional room ahead because the vehicle in front may roll backward slightly when starting.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing by vehicles in either direction except to make permitted turns.

question: What is the most common mistake drivers make when backing up?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Failing to look both ways (turning your head to check through the rear window) is the most common backing error; mirrors alone do not show everything.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,b:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas to slow down, and avoid heavy braking until control is regained; then pull off safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While in a travel lane on a roadway, which action is allowed?
options: a:Stop in the lane to look up an address.,b:Make a U-turn if you missed an exit.,c:Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.,d:Stop to drop off passengers.
note: Do not stop in a travel lane. Continue until you can safely pull off the roadway. If you miss an exit, proceed to the next one and turn around safely.

question: On slippery roads, you should:
options: a:Slow down,b:Drive faster than usual,c:Maintain the posted speed exactly
note: Reduce speed at the first sign of rain, sleet, or snow — sometimes slower than the posted limit is required for safety.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:You are moving faster than the bicyclist.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
note: Bicyclists may swerve to avoid road hazards and oncoming traffic may not see you beginning to pass. Give at least 3 feet of clearance and pass only when safe.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be secured?
options: a:Properly fastened in a child safety seat or seat belt appropriate for their size.,b:Held by a strong adult.,c:Standing on the floor in the back.,d:Seated without a restraint if the trip is short.
note: Children must be secured in appropriate child restraint systems; holding a child is not safe in the event of a crash.

question: What do pentagonal traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones or school crossings.,c:Speed limits.
note: A five-sided (pentagonal) sign warns of school zones and school crossings; be alert for children and reduced speeds.

question: Which color typically indicates a public recreation or cultural site on signs?
options: a:Orange,b:Green,c:Red
note: Brown is the official color for signs indicating cultural, historical, or recreational areas. (Note: brown is the correct color for these signs.)

question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right,b:Either one may go first,c:The vehicle on the right yields to the vehicle on the left
note: When two vehicles reach an intersection simultaneously, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: When is it important to slow down?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.,d:All of the above
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding roads, near intersections and crossings, and when road conditions (such as wet or icy surfaces) reduce traction.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Turn off the radio only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key.,c:Leave the engine running but lock the doors.,d:Just set the parking brake and leave.
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bike lanes?
options: a:Slow down, wait until oncoming traffic is clear, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Continue driving; it is the bicyclist’s responsibility to get out of the way.,c:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but leave at least 3 feet of clearance (more at higher speeds or for groups), and only pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right-hand lane?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not return to your lane until the entire vehicle you passed is visible in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:Yes, whenever safe.,b:No, except to turn into a driveway or make permitted turns.,c:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.,d:Only during daylight.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean you may not pass or change lanes. Crossing is allowed only to turn into or out of driveways or make permitted left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and back up.,b:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.,c:Continue to the next exit or other safe turnaround and use that to change direction.
note: Do not back up or make sudden lane changes on the freeway; proceed to the next exit or safe place to turn around.

question: What do downward-facing triangular signs usually mean?
options: a:School zone ahead.,b:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,c:Construction zone.,d:No passing zone.
note: A downward-pointing triangle indicates a yield sign—slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians as needed.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Combination solid and broken yellow,b:Single broken yellow,c:Double solid yellow
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction except to turn left when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, what steps should you take?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, signal, and re-enter the lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Honk your horn at least three times before passing.,c:Re-enter the lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,d:Pass without signaling if the lane is clear.
note: Before passing, check mirrors and blind spots, signal, complete the pass safely and return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle’s front in your rearview mirror.

question: May only vehicles with special plates or placards for persons with disabilities park in reserved spaces?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Spaces marked \Reserved Parking for Persons with Disabilities\" may be used only by vehicles displaying the appropriate plates or placards."

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and return safely to the missed exit.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,d:Roll down the window and ask for directions.
note: Do not back up or try to turn around on the highway. Continue to the next exit and turn around safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Do pedestrians always have the right-of-way in crosswalks and intersections?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when they are lawfully within a crosswalk or intersection; however, drivers must still exercise care to avoid collisions.

question: At a railroad crossing without warning signals, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed at normal speed because no train is near.,b:Slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains.,c:Honk and drive through quickly.,d:Stop only if a traffic light tells you to.
note: If a crossing lacks electric signals or gates, slow down, look both directions along the tracks, and listen before crossing.

question: Who is required to wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle in Nevada?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:All occupants of the vehicle.,c:Only adult passengers.,d:Only those in the front seats.
note: Nevada law requires all occupants of a moving vehicle to wear seat belts; special child restraint laws apply to young children.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect that could affect safety, when should you correct it?
options: a:As soon as possible.,b:Only when you can afford repairs.,c:Drive carefully and delay repairs.,d:Wait until the next scheduled maintenance.
note: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be corrected immediately before driving whenever possible.

question: Where are stop lines painted?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks to show where to stop.

question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle coming from the right has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle coming from the left has the right-of-way.,c:Whoever honks first
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles approaching from your right.

question: What best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,c:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.
note: Before backing, walk around and check behind the vehicle for children or obstacles; do not rely solely on mirrors.

question: May you drive around or under a lowering railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never drive around or under a lowering gate.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:If you first look carefully in both directions.
note: Do not drive around or under crossing gates; wait until lights and bells stop and gates are fully raised before crossing.

question: What device is often used on highways to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?
options: a:White lines on the side of the road.,b:Arrows painted or displayed to show turning lanes.,c:Flashing red lights.
note: Arrows (painted or displayed) indicate which lanes are for turning versus going straight.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and no passing is allowed.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and no passing is allowed.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is prohibited for vehicles in both directions.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed?
options: a:Go through as soon as the train passes.,b:Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.,c:Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
note: Do not proceed until you can see clearly down all tracks; another train may be approaching on a different track.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: After an upsetting incident at work, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving home,b:Drive fast to blow off steam,c:Play loud music to distract yourself
note: If you are emotionally upset, wait and calm down before driving; anger or strong emotions impair judgment and reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When drivers are on a road to your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.,c:When your traffic signal shows a green arrow.
note: You must yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. Also yield to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

question: When the road may be slippery, what is the safest action?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.,c:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: On slippery roads, reduce your speed, avoid cruise control, and increase following distance to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do several seconds before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Turn the wheel.,c:Use your signal.
note: Activate your turn signal about three to four seconds before turning to alert other road users.

question: What is the key principle for speed management when driving through curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve,b:Enter at the posted speed and then slow in the curve,c:Accelerate before entering the curve
note: Because inertia affects turning, reduce speed before entering a curve to maintain control and safety through the turn.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It causes hearing loss.,b:It increases pollution only.,c:It can allow carbon monoxide into the passenger compartment causing poisoning.
note: Exhaust leaks can let carbon monoxide and other toxic gases into the passenger area. Have any exhaust leaks repaired promptly to avoid poisoning.

question: If a road is covered with water, you should:
options: a:Turn around and find another route,b:Drive through carefully at low speed,c:Drive until water reaches the hubcaps
note: Never attempt to drive through flooded roadways — depth and current are unpredictable and can sweep vehicles away.

question: True or False: Cars begin to lose traction and can hydroplane at speeds of 70 mph.
options: a:True,b:False
note: False. Vehicles can lose traction and hydroplane at much lower speeds (often around 35 mph) on wet roads. Slow down in rain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and carefully continue through.,b:Stop fully, then proceed when the way is clear.,c:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.,d:Treat it like a yield sign and merge cautiously.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to go.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb required?
options: a:Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.,b:Is a good driving habit and is required by law.,c:Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
note: You must signal your intentions — the law requires signaling well in advance (at least 100 feet) before turning or changing lanes and before pulling from a curb.

question: Which best describes defensive driving?
options: a:Driving aggressively to assert right-of-way.,b:Using safe strategies to avoid crashes by adjusting to conditions.,c:Driving faster than others to reduce exposure time.,d:Avoiding using signals to prevent confusion.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and adjusting your driving for weather, fatigue, and other road users to prevent crashes.

question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, you should:
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can clear it completely,b:Move forward as far as possible to get closer to the front car,c:Go slowly until traffic ahead moves
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking intersections is illegal and causes gridlock.

question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Try to get out of their way and avoid eye contact.,b:Stare at the driver as they pass to teach them a lesson.,c:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,d:Challenge them by braking suddenly.
note: When confronted by an aggressive driver, make every effort to let them pass and avoid actions that might escalate the situation.

question: A steady yellow traffic light means:
options: a:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light is about to turn red,b:Speed up to clear the intersection,c:Stop immediately even if in the intersection
note: A steady yellow warns the signal will soon be red; if you can stop safely do so, otherwise cautiously clear the intersection.

question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The time of day.,b:Signal lights.,c:Road and pavement conditions.,d:The color of nearby vehicles.
note: Road conditions and pavement state greatly affect stopping ability. Reduce speed on slippery or damaged surfaces to maintain control.

question: What is a common cause of many crashes?
options: a:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors and blind spots.,b:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
note: Many crashes occur when drivers travel too fast for existing road or weather conditions; always adjust speed to the situation.

question: You may not parallel park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:15 feet,b:20 feet,c:30 feet
note: Parking too close to a fire hydrant is illegal; in Nevada you must not park within 15 feet of a hydrant.

question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look into the left side mirror.,b:Quickly glance over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,c:Look into the rearview mirror.
note: In addition to checking mirrors, look over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to verify there is no vehicle in your blind spot.

question: If two railroad tracks are side by side, what should you do after one train passes?
options: a:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.,b:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Look for a second train on the other track before crossing.
note: When multiple tracks exist, a second train may approach on the adjacent track. Wait until you are sure no trains are coming from either direction on any track before crossing.

question: Road surfaces become especially slippery when?
options: a:During the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm,b:After it has been raining for several hours,c:The day after it rains
note: Oil on the road surface rises to the top at the start of a rainstorm, making pavement particularly slick for the first 10–15 minutes.

question: True or false: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only at night,d:Only when other vehicles are present
note: You must use the proper turn signal any time you pull away from a curb to alert other road users.

question: A curb painted which color indicates a loading zone or other parking restriction?
options: a:Yellow,b:Blue,c:White
note: A yellow-painted curb typically designates a loading zone or other temporary parking restriction.

question: An octagonal road sign always indicates which instruction?
options: a:Stop,b:Hospital,c:Speed limit
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means stop — come to a complete stop when you approach it.

question: Which item does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much alcohol you drink.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.,d:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC depends on the amount consumed, body weight, and elapsed time between drinks. The beverage type does not change BAC once alcohol is in the bloodstream.

question: Hydroplaning is most commonly caused by:
options: a:Too much speed on wet roads causing tires to ride on water,b:Sudden stops,c:Worn windshield wipers
note: At higher speeds on wet pavement, tires can lose contact with the road and ride on a film of water, causing loss of steering control (hydroplaning).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow arrow signal?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected signal is ending; stop if you can do so safely unless already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is correct?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speed has no effect on crash severity.,c:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.,d:Driving faster always increases fuel efficiency.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than traffic can be dangerous. Higher speeds increase the chance of fatalities in crashes.

question: What color are highway guide signs that show directions and mileages?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Guide (destination) signs are green and provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above.
note: Always use turn signals to communicate when changing lanes, entering or leaving parking spaces, or pulling into traffic from alleys or parking areas.

question: If a vehicle starts to hydroplane (skid on water), should the driver immediately apply the brakes?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: If your vehicle hydroplanes, ease off the accelerator and steer to maintain control; do not slam on the brakes, which can worsen the skid.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A single broken yellow line separates opposite directions of traffic and indicates passing is allowed when it is safe.

question: To turn left from multilane one-way streets, you should begin your turn from which lane?
options: a:The left lane,b:The right lane,c:The center of the intersection
note: When turning left from a one-way street with multiple lanes, start from the left lane unless signs indicate otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: Move into the exit lane in advance and begin slowing after you are in the exit lane rather than on the main road.

question: When you approach a flashing yellow light, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Speed up to get past the hazard,c:Stop and wait for a green light
note: A flashing yellow light signals caution — slow down, look, and proceed carefully.

question: How far ahead should drivers look when traveling on a freeway?
options: a:10 seconds,b:20 to 30 seconds,c:15 seconds
note: On high-speed roadways, look 20 to 30 seconds ahead to anticipate traffic flow and hazards.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a collision, what should you do?
options: a:Not move your vehicle under any circumstances.,b:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway, if possible.,c:Wait until the police arrive before moving your vehicle.
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle out of the travel lanes if it is safe to do so; do not leave the scene without identifying yourself.

question: What do round traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Upcoming railroad crossings.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing so they can prepare to stop if necessary.

question: Which driving habit can help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually to avoid unnecessary stops,b:Accelerating quickly then coasting,c:Idling in your driveway with the engine running
note: Avoiding sudden stops and accelerating smoothly reduces fuel use; looking ahead to prevent unnecessary braking improves fuel economy.

question: If you are in the left lane and want to move right, what should you do before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles in the blind spot,b:Look over your left shoulder only,c:Signal and change lanes without checking mirrors
note: When changing lanes to the right, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your right shoulder to confirm the lane is clear.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:A designated no passing zone,b:A one-way traffic area,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle
note: 'No zones' are large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may disappear from the driver's view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after the vehicles ahead pass, what should you do?
options: a:Bring your vehicle to a complete stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,b:Proceed through without stopping again.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign because the way is clear.,d:Honk to warn any unseen traffic before proceeding.
note: You must stop fully at the stop sign each time and yield to any approaching traffic before proceeding.

question: When parallel parking, how close should your wheels be to the curb?
options: a:10 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches
note: When parallel parking, position your vehicle so your wheels are within 18 inches of the curb and do not block traffic visibility.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the road?
options: a:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,b:Slow down, regain control, and carefully steer back onto the pavement.,c:Stop on the shoulder and re-enter quickly.,d:Accelerate and yank the wheel to return.
note: If you drop onto a low shoulder, reduce speed without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.

question: When making an emergency roadside stop, is it necessary to set the parking brake?
options: a:True,b:False
note: True. When you stop on the side of the road in an emergency, set the parking brake and turn on your hazard lights to alert other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Maintain your normal driving speed.
note: You may turn on a steady green unless prohibited by sign, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

question: Where are U-turns prohibited?
options: a:On a hill with less than 500 feet visibility, in curves, or where posted prohibitions exist,b:Anywhere in a city,c:Only on highways with center barriers
note: U-turns are not permitted where visibility is under 500 feet on hills, in curves, or where signs prohibit them; otherwise they must be made safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal displays a steady green arrow, what does it permit?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,c:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow gives you protected movement in the arrow's direction, but you must yield to any pedestrians or vehicles already in the intersection.

question: Driving well under the posted speed limit is generally:
options: a:Potentially dangerous and can force others to take risks,b:Recommended at all times,c:Always safe
note: Driving significantly below the posted limit can disrupt traffic flow and cause other drivers to take unsafe actions to pass.

question: A diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicates what?
options: a:A warning about potential hazards or changes in road conditions,b:A school zone,c:A recreational area
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of existing or possible hazards ahead; they are usually yellow (or orange in work zones).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Keep your speed and ignore the backup.,c:Speed up suddenly to clear the way.,d:Turn on hazard lights and continue slowly.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving much slower than the flow, pull off the road where safe and let other vehicles pass.

question: When is parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder permitted?
options: a:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergency situations; use hazards and call for help if needed.

question: How does increasing your vehicle’s speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It increases your field of vision.,b:It decreases your field of vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.
note: As speed increases, your effective field of vision narrows, reducing your ability to see hazards off to the sides. Slow down to increase awareness.

question: Which is true about driving on wet pavement?
options: a:Roads are most slippery just after rain begins.,b:Hydroplaning can occur on wet roads.,c:You should allow additional stopping distance.,d:All of the above.
note: Wet roads can be especially slick right after rain begins, may cause hydroplaning, and require extra stopping distance and caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you prepare to drive to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Only have to know generally where your destination is.,b:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,c:Should plan your trip in advance.
note: Plan your route in advance and review maps or directions before you start driving in unfamiliar areas.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Drivers cannot see as well at night.,b:Traffic always moves faster at night.,c:There is more volume of traffic at night.,d:Headlights are not needed after midnight.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it harder to see hazards; headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.

question: What does a 'No standing' sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.,b:You may stop temporarily only to pickup or discharge passengers.,c:You may never stop your vehicle there.
note: A 'No standing' sign allows stopping temporarily only to load or unload passengers; parking or waiting is not permitted.

question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with functioning lights, you should:
options: a:Follow the officer's directions rather than the traffic signal,b:Follow whatever the traffic light indicates,c:Ignore the officer and follow other drivers
note: Officer directions supersede traffic signals; obey the officer's hand signals and commands for safety and legal compliance.

question: Is it lawful for a car to share a single lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane. A car must not try to share the same lane with a motorcycle.

question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving are likely to:
options: a:Have no driving errors.,b:Be more distracted and have trouble controlling their vehicle.,c:Drive better because they are satisfied.,d:Become more alert and focused.
note: Eating or drinking while driving distracts hands and eyes, increasing the likelihood of lane deviations and control errors.

question: A broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line.
note: If the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may pass when it is safe; if the solid line is on your side, you may not pass.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: To check the blind spot in the direction you intend to move, glance over that shoulder in addition to checking mirrors and signaling.

question: What type of sign is normally diamond-shaped and warns of hazards ahead?
options: a:Warning sign.,b:Interstate route sign.,c:School crossing sign.,d:Regulatory sign
note: Warning signs are typically diamond-shaped and alert drivers to upcoming hazards or special conditions.

question: If you are traveling in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Remain in the blind spot and maintain speed.,b:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you.,c:Flash your headlights continuously.,d:Sound your horn repeatedly to warn the other driver.
note: Do not drive in someone else’s blind spot. Either move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: Which safety restraints provide the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Only an airbag.,b:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,c:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,d:Only a child restraint seat.
note: Safety belts plus airbags provide the greatest protection. Always wear both the lap and shoulder belt and use child seats as required.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do if you are not involved?
options: a:Keep moving and pay attention to driving.,b:Keep moving without changing speed.,c:Stop to look at the scene so you can help.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely render aid. Keep your attention on driving and watch for people near the roadway.

question: What is the standard top-to-bottom order of lights on a vertically arranged traffic signal?
options: a:Red, green, yellow.,b:Red, yellow, green.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On a vertical traffic signal the lights are arranged red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, your first step should be to:
options: a:Pull up parallel to the car in front of the desired space,b:Turn your wheels immediately to the left,c:Turn your wheels to the right first
note: After selecting a space, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space, signal, and then back or steer into the spot as appropriate.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph take to stop?
options: a:50 feet,b:125 feet,c:400 feet
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers require much greater stopping distance than passenger cars and can take nearly 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the wheel opposite the direction of the skid.,c:Keep the front wheels straight.,d:Turn sharply into the shoulder to stop the skid.
note: When skidding, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to travel. As it straightens, correct steering to regain control.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,c:It has no effect on driving abilities.,d:It only impairs judgment at high amounts.
note: Alcohol impairs many driving abilities including reaction time, vision, speed and distance judgment, and decision-making.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Extremely risky behavior,b:Rare and usually harmless,c:Not a serious concern
note: Distracted driving greatly increases crash risk for drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and other road users; focus on driving to prevent crashes.

question: Before backing out of a driveway near children at play, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of the vehicle and walk to the rear to ensure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn loudly while reversing.,c:Rev the engine to get attention.,d:Rely only on mirrors to check behind you.
note: When children are nearby, exit the vehicle and check behind it before backing out. Do not depend solely on mirrors.

question: Is it true that alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Alcohol impairs vision and reaction time and is the leading contributing factor in fatal crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you merge onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to traffic already on the freeway.,b:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match the speed of freeway traffic.,c:Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.,d:All of the above.
note: When entering freeway traffic use the ramp to accelerate to freeway speed, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to traffic already on the freeway.

question: If your turn signals stop working, what should you use to indicate a turn?
options: a:Your horn.,b:Your headlights.,c:Hand signals.,d:Flash your emergency lights only.
note: If turn signals fail, use the standard hand signals to indicate your intentions to other road users.

question: What is the correct action when approaching railroad tracks?
options: a:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,b:Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop.,c:Speed up to cross the tracks before the gate is lowered.
note: Approach railroad crossings cautiously: look and listen for trains and be prepared to stop for any approaching rail traffic.

question: Which action most reliably prevents alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply say “No thanks, I'm driving” if offered a drink.,c:Call a taxi after you begin drinking.
note: The safest way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide beforehand not to drive after drinking. Alcohol impairs judgment, so planning in advance is critical.

question: How much longer can stopping distances be on slippery roads compared with dry pavement?
options: a:About the same as on dry pavement.,b:A little shorter than on dry pavement.,c:Two to ten times longer than on dry pavement.,d:Less than on dry pavement if you have anti-lock brakes.
note: On slippery roads, stopping distances can be two to ten times longer than on dry pavement; use extra caution and slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it unlawful to cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When doing so would interfere with traffic.,b:Only when turning into a driveway.,c:When the car in front of you is disabled.,d:It is always unlawful to cross broken lines.
note: You may cross a broken line to pass or change lanes so long as it can be done safely and without interfering with traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your car end up?
options: a:In the left lane of the one-way street.,b:In the center of the street.,c:In the right lane of the one-way street.,d:Any available lane as long as it is safe.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, enter the lane closest to the one you left—typically the left lane of the one-way street, but Nevada guidance indicates completing the turn into the lane closest to your prior lane; choose the lane nearest your approach to avoid crossing lanes.

question: What do orange-colored signs typically indicate?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:School zone signs.
note: Orange signs are generally used in highway work zones to warn drivers of workers and unusual conditions ahead.

question: Are traffic signs and pavement markings mandatory or optional?
options: a:Are merely suggestions.,b:Must always be obeyed.,c:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and must be obeyed.

question: What are the colors of warning signs indicating upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white.,b:Black symbols or letters on yellow.,c:White on blue.,d:Green on white.
note: General warning signs are yellow with black symbols or lettering. Work zone warnings are orange with black symbols.

question: If you stop along the road at night, how should you make your vehicle visible?
options: a:Turn off all your lights.,b:Use your headlights only.,c:Turn on your emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.
note: When stopped at night, use your emergency flashers and leave low-beam headlights on so other drivers can see you.

question: How can you avoid drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals for a rest.,b:Turning on your car radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Plan regular stops to rest and stretch during long trips to prevent fatigue-related driving impairment.

question: What must you do when pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk?
options: a:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.,b:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.,c:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
note: Marked crosswalks give pedestrians the right-of-way; you must stop and allow them to cross safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield.,c:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the edge of the road and stopping when safe.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement means:
options: a:Drivers in the lane must make the movement shown by the arrow.,b:Drivers may choose whether to follow the arrow.,c:Only follow the arrow if a traffic light is not working.,d:Stop before proceeding in the arrow's direction.
note: A pavement arrow indicates the required movement from that lane; follow it unless directed otherwise by signs or signals.

question: What is the best way to reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.,c:Watch for standing water and avoid it when safe.,d:All of the above.
note: Maintain tires, slow down in wet conditions, and watch out for standing water to reduce hydroplaning risk. Do not use cruise control in wet conditions.

question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed strategy?
options: a:Drive at the speed of the flow of traffic within the posted limit.,b:Drive faster than the flow of traffic to avoid congestion.,c:Drive much slower than other traffic to stay safe.,d:Constantly fluctuate speed to stay alert.
note: Driving with the flow of traffic, within the posted limit, reduces crash risk from speed differentials.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road to let them pass.,b:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them complete the pass safely.,c:Speed up to prevent them passing.,d:Brake suddenly to discourage them.
note: When passed on the left, remain right and adjust speed or position to give the passing vehicle room to return to your lane safely.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway from the right lane to the left, you should:
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your left shoulder for the blind spot, and signal,b:Only signal and move over,c:Rely solely on the side mirror
note: Always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to verify the blind spot is clear, and signal.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn sharply toward the curb.,b:Turn slightly to the right.,c:Turn sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked uphill with a curb, turn the wheels sharply away from the curb so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves. On an uphill without a curb, turn wheels toward the edge of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about advisory or posted speed signs is correct?
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:They have a triangular shape.,c:They are blue with black lettering.
note: Advisory speed signs give recommended speeds for curves or conditions; drivers should reduce speed below the advisory in rain, snow, or ice. (Note: advisory speeds should not be exceeded in adverse conditions.)

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who has the right-of-way when a funeral procession is present?
options: a:A pedestrian,b:The funeral procession,c:Another driver
note: Motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians must yield to vehicles in a funeral procession; procession vehicles may follow through intersections together.

question: Anything that causes you to ____ could lead to a crash.
options: a:Take your hands off the wheel,b:Take your attention away from the task of driving,c:Take your eyes off the road
note: Distractions that remove your attention from driving, your hands from the wheel, or your eyes from the road increase the risk of crashing.

question: Vehicle stopping distances never depend on which factor?
options: a:Your own reaction time.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brake condition, tires, speed, and road conditions, but not directly on the time of day.

question: In rain, which headlights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.,d:Hazard lights at all times.
note: Use low-beam headlights in rainy conditions. High beams can reflect off rain and reduce visibility.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a vehicle to drive?
options: a:Your seat belt,b:The steering wheel,c:Your rearview mirror
note: Adjust your seating position first so you can reach controls and see clearly; then adjust mirrors and steering wheel as needed. (Note: the recommended order is seat, mirrors, then steering wheel.)

question: What type of situation does an orange-colored sign indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone.,c:A railroad crossing.,d:A recreational area.
note: Orange signs with black lettering warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations and require extra caution.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Add extra weight to the vehicle.,b:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,c:Get off highways quickly at all costs.,d:Use only parking lights.
note: Reducing speed and increasing following distance are key to avoiding crashes on snow- or ice-covered roads.

question: When approaching a school bus stopped with its stop-arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk before passing to warn children.,c:Slow down and pass cautiously.,d:Pass on the shoulder if no children are visible.
note: Stop for a school bus using its stop signal and remain stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and it is safe to proceed.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause which danger to occupants?
options: a:Make you drowsy or expose you to toxic fumes,b:Increase tire wear,c:Cause brake failure
note: Exhaust leaks can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic gases into the vehicle cabin, causing drowsiness, poisoning, or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you respond to a flashing red traffic light at an intersection?
options: a:Come to a full stop and proceed when it is safe.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop completely, yield to others, and go only when the way is clear.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus when driving on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On two-lane roads drivers in both directions must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and stop arm extended.

question: Before driving an unfamiliar borrowed vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Take a moment to locate and test signals, lights, wipers, and brakes.,b:Assume it operates the same as your car and drive immediately.,c:Hide defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,d:Only check the radio and seat position.
note: When driving an unfamiliar car, familiarize yourself with key controls and ensure any defects are corrected before driving.

question: What should you do to help prevent crashes with other road users?
options: a:Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.,b:Ignore other drivers and focus only on your lane.,c:Drive only on side streets.,d:Use hazards instead of turn signals.
note: Communicate intentions with signals, horn, and appropriate lights so other road users can anticipate your actions and avoid collisions.

question: True or false: You must yield to children playing in the street.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if a parent is present,d:Only during daytime
note: Drive with extreme caution where children may be present; slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

question: How should a seat belt fit?
options: a:Loose across the abdomen.,b:Buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen with the shoulder belt comfortable.,c:Hidden under your coat for comfort.,d:Only across the chest.
note: Lap belts should sit across the hip bones and lower abdomen and shoulder belts should be snug but comfortable across the chest.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, under which condition must you always stop?
options: a:If a stop sign is posted.,b:If the crossing gate is lowered or warning lights flash.,c:Only if you hear a train.,d:Only if flaggers are present.
note: Stop if flashing red lights activate, a crossing gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals stop, or if a train is visible or too close to cross safely.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your high beams.,b:Use your low beams.,c:Use your parking lights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low-beam headlights to improve visibility and reduce glare that high beams cause by reflecting off moisture.

question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Wear your seat belt.,c:Limit your driving to weekdays.
note: Wearing a seat belt is the most effective way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash.

question: If you see an animal on the roadway, you should:
options: a:Use extreme caution and pass slowly to avoid startling it,b:Pass as close as possible,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly
note: Approach animals on the road with care and pass slowly to avoid startling or causing unpredictable movement.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:White.,b:Green.,c:Yellow.,d:Blue.
note: Yellow centerlines separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Help the injured.,b:Call the police.,c:Stop immediately.
note: Stop immediately, move your vehicle out of traffic if possible, render aid when safe, and call the police or ambulance if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, how often must you signal?
options: a:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,b:Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: You should always signal when turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb; signaling helps other drivers and pedestrians anticipate your actions.

question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your first legal obligation?
options: a:Stop.,b:Call the police.,c:Determine if anyone is injured.
note: You must stop at the scene of a crash. If anyone is injured, call 911; you must report crashes meeting Nevada reporting thresholds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a motorist is making a left turn at an intersection, must they yield to an oncoming bicyclist?
options: a:True: Yes, yield to oncoming bicyclists.,b:False: Bicyclists must yield.,c:Only if the bicyclist is on the sidewalk.,d:Only at marked bike lanes.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming bicyclists just as they would to oncoming motor vehicles.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol's effect on driving abilities?
options: a:Only very high BAC reduces concentration.,b:Alcohol does not reduce concentration.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can reduce concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.,d:Small amounts improve reaction time.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol reduce concentration, perception, judgment and memory, impairing driving skills.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:Provide information for drivers.,b:Are usually not important.,c:Are only found in construction zones.
note: Pavement markings guide lane positioning, show safe passing areas, and warn of upcoming conditions—obey them.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what is the safest response?
options: a:Pull up beside them and confront them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams repeatedly to warn them.,d:Follow closely to teach them a lesson.
note: To avoid escalating incidents and road rage, let the event go and continue driving safely without responding aggressively.

question: If your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Leave a written note with your name, address, and the circumstances of the accident,b:Drive away after reporting it when convenient,c:Wait for the police to arrive regardless
note: If you collide with an unattended vehicle, leave your contact information and details of the incident where the owner can find it.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens?
options: a:It speeds up your reactions.,b:It makes you overconfident and slows reactions.,c:It makes you more cautious.,d:It metabolizes faster improving coordination.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and slows reaction times, often increasing confidence and leading to more driving errors.

question: True or false: Since driving involves risk, you should continually improve driving and observation skills.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if you are a new driver.,d:Only for professional drivers
note: Drivers should continually practice and improve observation and driving skills to reduce risk.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane at a reduced speed.,b:Slow down and continue if it is in another lane.,c:Pull to the right curb and stop until it passes.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: Upon seeing or hearing an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right and stop, allowing it to pass and following any on-scene instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:On a hill or curve, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.,b:Only on multi-lane highways.,c:Only when behind a school bus.,d:Only during poor weather.
note: Do not pass on hills, curves, intersections, bridges, or railroad crossings, or where signs prohibit passing.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, which action is recommended?
options: a:Sit in the car and wait without signaling.,b:Use your four-way flashers, pull off the road if possible, and signal before exiting.,c:Sound your horn to attract attention.,d:Stop in the travel lane until help arrives.
note: When disabled on a highway, signal, move as far off the road as possible, turn on hazard flashers, and lift the hood to indicate trouble.

question: If you have a tire blowout, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Brake hard immediately and pull off quickly.,b:Take your foot off the gas, do not brake immediately, gradually slow and pull off the road.,c:Accelerate to stabilize the vehicle.,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to the shoulder.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the gas, avoid immediate hard braking, gradually reduce speed, then steer to a safe location and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it required to use your turn signal?
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,d:All of the above.
note: Use your turn signals for any movement left or right, when changing lanes, entering traffic from parking areas, and when pulling into/out of parking spaces.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so a rollaway will not enter traffic.

question: When may drivers use a cell phone while driving?
options: a:Only when using a hands-free accessory,b:Never under any circumstances,c:At any time in any manner
note: Handheld voice communications while driving are prohibited unless using an approved hands-free accessory; texting and other non-voice uses are forbidden.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means recognizing potential hazards and taking proactive steps to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When interacting with pedestrians, which is required of drivers?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle.,b:Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is in the wrong.,c:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.
note: Drivers must yield and take actions to avoid striking pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is not following rules.

question: Should the stereo volume be so loud that you cannot hear traffic?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Keep stereo volume low enough to hear important outside sounds like horns, sirens, and other traffic warnings.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed you are traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The pavement condition.,d:All of the above.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brake and tire condition, and the road surface—among other factors like vehicle weight and reaction time.

question: If an officer suspects you of driving under the influence, what is true about testing?
options: a:Can always refuse to be tested for the presence of controlled substances.,b:Cannot refuse to be tested for the presence of controlled substances.,c:Can refuse to be tested for the presence of substances if it is your first offense.
note: Under Nevada's implied consent law, refusal to submit to authorized chemical tests can result in license revocation and other penalties.

question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles already on the public road,b:Expect drivers on the road to yield to them,c:Force their way into traffic if necessary
note: Yield to traffic on the public roadway when entering from a driveway or private road and merge when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually the best practice?
options: a:Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic so you can merge smoothly. Vehicles already on the freeway have the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor greatly increases stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:High speeds.,b:Slow speeds.,c:Night driving.,d:Driving in rain only.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the force of impact, making crashes more severe.

question: On a one-way street when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop,b:Speed up to get out of the way,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving
note: On a one-way street, you must move to the nearest roadside and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren.

question: If you are being tailgated and there is no right lane, how should you react?
options: a:Speed up so the tailgater goes around you.,b:Slow down when safe to create space ahead and encourage them to pass.,c:Brake abruptly to warn them.,d:Stop in your lane immediately.
note: If you are tailgated and cannot move right, gradually reduce speed when safe to allow the tailgater to pass. Never brake abruptly.

question: When may you use a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:When your vehicle has multiple occupants.,b:When you are driving faster than other traffic.,c:When driving more slowly than traffic.,d:When towing a trailer.
note: HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles with multiple occupants and are marked with signs and diamond pavement symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a steady yellow traffic light?
options: a:Accelerate to clear the intersection before it turns red.,b:Slow to a stop unless you are already within the intersection.,c:Continue at the same speed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Stop immediately even if in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon be red; stop if you can do so safely and you are not already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When vehicles arrive at the same time at an open intersection, yield to the vehicle on your right and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and there is adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a shared center lane be used on a roadway with traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:To pass other vehicles.,b:To slow down or stop before making a left turn.,c:As an additional travel lane when traffic is slow.
note: A center turn lane is intended for making or preparing to make left turns. It is not for passing or general travel.

question: Which of the following is an effect of consuming alcoholic beverages?
options: a:It impairs thinking, reaction time, and coordination.,b:It improves night vision.,c:It sharpens judgment.
note: Alcohol depresses brain functions that control judgment, inhibition, coordination, balance, vision, and reaction time.

question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what is true?
options: a:You may still turn in the arrow's direction but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic,b:You may turn with absolute right-of-way,c:You may no longer turn in that direction under any circumstance
note: When a green arrow ends and a steady green remains, you may still turn but must yield to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles.

question: Which of the following statements about winter driving is not true?
options: a:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,b:Checking your vehicle's antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels is especially important during the winter.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is a safe thing to do.
note: Do not use cruise control in snow, rain, or icy conditions; winter driving requires extra caution and vehicle maintenance.

question: Regulatory signs are used to:
options: a:Indicate what drivers must or must not do in a designated area,b:Warn of potential hazards ahead,c:Provide directions to nearby services
note: Regulatory signs (often white with black markings) set legal requirements such as speed limits, no-turn zones, and lane use.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your high beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Do not use high beams in fog; they reflect off the fog and reduce visibility—use low beams instead.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,c:You become more alert.,d:Your ability to recover from headlight glare is reduced.
note: Alcohol reduces reaction time, distorts judgment of speed and distance, reduces alertness, and impairs recovery from glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A green arrow pointing left,c:A solid green light.
note: A steady green arrow pointing left gives you the protected right-of-way to turn in the arrow's direction.

question: When changing lanes, what actions are important?
options: a:Signal, check your blind spot, and ensure the lane is clear before moving,b:Only signal and immediately move,c:Make a sudden lane change to avoid slow traffic
note: Signal early, check mirrors and your blind spot, and confirm the lane is clear before making the lane change.

question: How can you avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:Quickly turn your head and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.,b:Adjust your mirrors every mile.,c:Honk briefly before moving.,d:Rely solely on mirrors to check blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes or turning, glance over your shoulder toward the direction of travel to check blind spots rather than relying only on mirrors.

question: What is hardest to see at night?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Pedestrians.,c:Road signs.
note: Pedestrians are often the hardest objects to see at night compared with road signs and other vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a 'No stopping' sign permit you to do?
options: a:To discharge passengers.,b:To avoid conflict with other traffic.,c:Long enough to unload packages.
note: A 'No stopping' sign allows stopping only to obey a traffic control device, a police officer, or to avoid a traffic conflict.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an oncoming vehicle is in your lane headed toward you, what should you do first?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and accelerate.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake firmly.,d:Flash your lights and maintain your lane.
note: If a vehicle is approaching head-on in your lane, warn with your horn, try to avoid a collision by escaping to the right, and brake firmly if needed.

question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway,b:Always make a complete stop even when no traffic is present,c:Yield only to traffic on your right
note: A yield sign requires slowing and giving the right-of-way to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway you plan to enter.

question: When making a turn, what should you generally do to your speed?
options: a:Reduce speed so you can remain in control and stay in your lane,b:Increase speed to complete the turn faster,c:Maintain the exact same speed
note: Reduce speed before and during a turn to maintain control, stay in your lane, and respond to unexpected hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By looking in your rearview mirror.,c:By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots cannot be seen in mirrors; turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check them.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give as much lateral space as possible,b:Honk continuously before passing,c:Drive into the bicycle lane to pass more quickly
note: Give bicyclists ample space and slow down when passing; do not crowd or force them off the road.

question: True or False: Ramps and bridges freeze before the main highway and road surfaces.
options: a:True,b:False
note: True. Ramps and bridges can ice before other roadway surfaces because they are exposed to cold air on all sides. Use extra caution crossing them in freezing conditions.

question: Must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
