note: Drivers are required to stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and stop arm extended, whether on public or private roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate and changing lanes, what must you do?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.,b:Always use cruise control when changing lanes.,c:Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.,d:Change lanes without signaling in light traffic.
note: On interstates, signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before lane changes. Use shoulders only in emergencies and limit lane changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using lights or siren, you do not need to clear the lane; continue normally.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: If you see a lane with a solid line on your side and a broken line on the other, may you pass?
options: a:True,b:False
note: If the solid line is on your side, you may not pass; only the side with the broken line may pass when safe.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance and make sure headlights are working properly.,b:Drive with no headlights to reduce glare.,c:Always use high beams regardless of oncoming traffic.,d:Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of visibility.
note: At night, increase following distance, avoid fatigue, and ensure headlights are functioning properly to enhance safety.

question: A sound rule for passing is to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe,b:Pass on the right whenever possible,c:Always try to get to the front of slow traffic
note: Limit passing to necessary, legal, and safe situations and travel with the flow rather than constantly passing.

question: If you are upset, nervous, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive as you would normally since emotions don't affect driving.,b:Take time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.,c:Drive faster to get where you are going quickly.,d:Listen to loud music to feel better while driving.
note: Strong emotions impair driving ability. Take time to calm and focus before operating a vehicle.

question: What helps you avoid emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk to warn drivers ahead.,b:Look ahead and keep a safe following distance.,c:Drive only in the right lane.,d:Constantly change lanes to avoid slowdowns.
note: Scanning ahead and maintaining a safe following distance reduce the need for sudden stops and the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: How can you relieve fatigue during a long drive?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Chew gum continuously.,c:Drive with one eye closed at a time.,d:Open all windows and drive faster.
note: On long trips, stop for short breaks every two hours. If drowsy, pull safely off the road and rest or find lodging.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, or smoking.,b:Talking or texting on a phone.,c:Changing radio stations or CDs.,d:All of the above.
note: Any activity that diverts attention from driving—eating, using a phone, or adjusting audio—can be dangerous.

question: Is it unlawful to drive at night using only parking lights?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Parking lights alone are not sufficient for night driving; headlights are required when visibility is low.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you allow?
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Demand the other driver pull over.,d:Always back up to the nearest driveway.
note: On narrow roads, drivers must allow oncoming vehicles at least one-half of the main traveled portion so both can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At an intersection with a stop sign.,b:Where there is a red light.,c:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,d:In all of these situations.
note: You must stop at stop signs, red lights (including flashing red), and whenever a police or other authorized traffic officer orders you to stop.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, do not retaliate, and distance yourself from the situation,b:Make eye contact to assert yourself,c:Respond with hand gestures
note: If other drivers display road rage, distance yourself by slowing and moving over safely; avoid engaging or escalating the situation.

question: What may occur when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:Nothing will happen.,b:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.,c:The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify the impairing effects of both substances and create unpredictable results.

question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Stop and wait for cross traffic.,b:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and turn if permitted.,c:Always turn without yielding.,d:Reverse out of the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may go through the intersection when it is clear; turning drivers must still yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light means you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Increase speed to clear the intersection.,d:Yield to oncoming traffic only.
note: A flashing yellow light indicates you should slow down and proceed carefully.

question: The space you require to cross traffic depends on:
options: a:Road and weather conditions and oncoming traffic,b:Whether there is a stop sign,c:Whether you used your turn signal
note: The gap needed to cross or turn depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, must drivers yield to motorists who arrived before them?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: At a multi-way stop vehicles should proceed in the order of arrival; yield to any vehicle that arrived before you.

question: Is it legal to drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Never drive around, under, or through lowered gates or crossing barriers — it's illegal and extremely dangerous.

question: Roads freeze most quickly where they are:
options: a:Shaded by trees or buildings (in the sun they may stay warmer),b:Flat and exposed to full sun,c:Curvy with lots of traffic
note: Shaded sections freeze before other areas and are the last to dry; use extra caution on shaded spots in cold weather.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater crash risk when using which device?
options: a:Cell phone,b:Radio,c:CD player
note: Using a cell phone (including hands-free) significantly increases crash risk; any audio device can also distract the driver.

question: If a vehicle equipped with ABS starts to skid on a slippery road, what should the driver do?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.
note: With Anti-Lock Braking Systems, press and hold the brake pedal firmly; the ABS will automatically modulate braking to help maintain control while you steer out of danger.

question: How close may you legally park to a crosswalk?
options: a:20 feet,b:40 feet,c:30 feet
note: Do not park within 20 feet of a pedestrian crosswalk at an intersection so pedestrians remain visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before passing on a multilane highway?
options: a:Pass only on the right.,b:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Ensure the passing lane is clear and that the maneuver can be completed safely before you signal and change lanes.

question: Are headlights legally required when people or vehicles cannot be seen at 1,000 feet?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Headlights must be used from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and whenever people or vehicles are not clearly visible at 1,000 feet.

question: When approaching a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Slow down and yield to pedestrians and traffic, stopping if necessary,b:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear,c:Have automatic right-of-way
note: Slow and be prepared to stop at a yield sign; proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely:
options: a:A blind person.,b:Part of a traffic study.,c:A deaf person.,d:A crossing guard.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For how far may drivers travel in a center turn lane before making a left turn?
options: a:100 feet.,b:50 feet.,c:200 feet.
note: You may travel no more than 200 feet in a center left-turn lane before making your left turn. Center turn lanes are for turning only, not travel lanes.

question: How are crosswalks indicated?
options: a:Always indicated by vertical pavement markings.,b:Always indicated by horizontal pavement markings.,c:Either indicated by pavement markings or are not marked at all.
note: Crosswalks may be marked or unmarked at intersections; drivers must yield to pedestrians in either case.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed that is:
options: a:The maximum speed limit.,b:Faster than is reasonable and prudent.,c:Safe for existing conditions.
note: You must not drive at a speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions. Adjust your speed for weather, traffic, road, and visibility conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Coming to a complete stop, yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when clear describes the meaning of which signal?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means stop (like a stop sign), yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

question: In fog, which headlight use is correct?
options: a:Use low beams and drive cautiously; do not use high beams,b:Use high beams to see farther ahead,c:Turn off headlights and use parking lights
note: High beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility. Use low beams (or fog lights) and reduce speed when driving in fog.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and slash over a black symbol mean?
options: a:Drivers must stop.,b:The action shown is forbidden.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol indicates that the depicted action is prohibited.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your four-way flashers.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beam),d:Do not use any lights.
note: You must turn on headlights at dusk or in poor visibility and use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet when following another vehicle.

question: What should you do when driving in foggy conditions?
options: a:Turn on your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: Use low-beam headlights (not high beams) in fog to improve visibility; reduce speed and be prepared to stop if visibility worsens.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It prevents drivers from changing lanes.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,c:It increases travel speed.,d:It eliminates the need for mirrors.
note: Leaving space around your vehicle ensures you have time to react to mistakes by other drivers or sudden hazards.

question: On non-freeway roads, drivers should look at least how many seconds ahead?
options: a:12 seconds,b:5 seconds,c:10 seconds
note: On regular roads drivers should scan about 12 seconds — farther on freeways — to anticipate hazards and avoid sudden maneuvers.

question: On a road that has no sidewalks, which direction should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:On the side facing oncoming traffic.,b:On the side where traffic is lightest.,c:In the same direction as the traffic flow.,d:In the middle of the lane to be more visible.
note: Where there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the edge of the roadway facing oncoming traffic so they can see and react to approaching vehicles.

question: If railroad crossing signals are flashing as you approach, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail while the signals warn of a train.,c:Look for a train and then speed up to clear the track.,d:Proceed if no train is visible.
note: When electric or mechanical signals are warning of a train, stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until it is safe to cross.

question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the road between the cars.,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may miss their turn signals.,d:It reduces your fuel efficiency.
note: Following too closely reduces your time to react and stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: What is the most common color used for warning signs?
options: a:Yellow,b:Red,c:Green
note: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering to warn of unexpected conditions.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for hazards ahead?
options: a:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,b:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,c:Stare straight ahead at all times.
note: Continuously scan far ahead and to the sides to detect hazards early and give yourself time to react.

question: How does distracted driving usually affect your reaction to hazards?
options: a:It causes you to react more slowly.,b:It makes you react faster.,c:It has no effect.,d:It improves focus on driving tasks.
note: Distracted driving slows a driver's reaction time and reduces attention to the roadway, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,c:The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions. You must drive more slowly when conditions (weather, traffic, visibility) make the posted speed unsafe.

question: Which practice does NOT help promote safe night driving?
options: a:Relying on tinted windows that reduce night visibility,b:Keeping the windshield clean,c:Carrying a flashlight
note: Tinted windows reduce visibility at night and can make driving more hazardous; keep glass clean and carry a flashlight to increase safety.

question: If you must slow on a slippery road, what is the first thing you should do?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, first remove your foot from the accelerator. If you need to slow more, apply the brake gradually and steadily.

question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Sound your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians.,c:Use your emergency lights only.,d:Shout at the other driver.
note: Use your horn to alert other drivers or pedestrians when you believe a collision is imminent.

question: What do pennant-shaped signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Pennant-shaped signs typically mark the start of a no-passing zone; text on the sign will confirm this.

question: What color are signs that show distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Green with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Red with white letters.,d:Blue with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are typically green with white lettering or symbols.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:Are passing a bicyclist.,b:See a child who is about to run into the street.,c:Are traveling through an intersection.
note: Use your horn as a warning to alert others of imminent danger, for example if a child is about to run into the street.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cross lanes to reach the exit.,b:Make a U-turn on the interstate.,c:Continue to the next exit and use it to return.,d:Reverse on the shoulder to the exit.
note: If you pass your exit, continue to the next one. Do not make abrupt lane changes, U-turns, or reverse on the highway.

question: What is a key trait of a good defensive driver?
options: a:Driving slowly at all times.,b:Anticipating and watching for actions of other drivers.,c:Keeping a constant speed regardless of conditions.,d:Showing impatience with slow drivers.
note: A defensive driver watches for other drivers' actions and anticipates problems to avoid collisions.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't endanger your driving?
options: a:Know how any medications affect your driving.,b:Drive despite physical limitations to maintain schedule.,c:Ignore prescribed limits.,d:Only drive when perfectly fit every day.
note: Be aware of how medicines and your physical condition affect driving, and only drive within your capabilities.

question: Does a double solid yellow centerline permit passing in either direction?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Double solid yellow lines mean passing is prohibited for traffic traveling in either direction.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right toward the curb.,b:Turn your wheels to the left toward traffic.,c:Keep wheels straight ahead.,d:Turn wheels sharply away from the curb.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb so a rollback will move the vehicle away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,d:Both oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and to pedestrians and other road users already in the intersection.

question: Which of these statements about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:Not all crossings have gates or signals, and it is illegal to go around lowered gates,b:You may always drive around a gate if no train is visible,c:You never have to stop at a railroad crossing
note: Some crossings lack active warning devices; obey flaggers and never go around lowered gates — it is illegal and dangerous.

question: Which is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers,b:Human error,c:Bad weather
note: Human error—such as inattention, misjudgment, or failure to follow laws—is the most common factor in crashes.

question: About how many standard alcoholic drinks does the average body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three drinks an hour.,b:One drink an hour.,c:Two drinks an hour.
note: On average, the body processes roughly one standard drink per hour, though many factors (weight, food, health) affect impairment and elimination rate.

question: What should you do before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.,b:Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.,c:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.
note: Always look and listen for approaching trains from both directions and observe any signals; only cross when it is safe to do so.

question: Signs that warn of hazardous conditions ahead are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Warning signs advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions or changes in the roadway; obey them for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Yield to vehicles approaching from the right and be prepared to yield to avoid a crash.,c:Stop at the intersection regardless of traffic.,d:Always let the largest vehicle go first.
note: When there is no control device, yield to traffic from the right and be prepared to yield to avoid collisions. Scan left-right-left again before proceeding.

question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:If traffic is clear.
note: When the broken line is adjacent to your lane, you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: How should you approach turns when roads are slick?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Take turns more slowly than usual.,c:Change lanes quickly.
note: On slick roads reduce your speed when approaching and negotiating turns to maintain control and traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:See if you can reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up to you.,b:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights; pull to the right edge of the road and stop when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and ensuring it is safe to proceed.,b:After slowing down to verify no cross traffic.,c:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,d:Without stopping if no other cars are present.
note: If there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Must drivers yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly?
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must do everything reasonably possible to avoid striking a pedestrian, yielding as necessary to prevent injury.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are likely a police officer.,c:They are visually impaired and may not see your vehicle.,d:They will always yield to cars.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind pedestrian. Slow, yield, and be prepared to stop to prevent injury.

question: When stopped in a line crossing a railroad track with no signals, what must you ensure before entering the tracks?
options: a:You have enough space ahead to clear the tracks without stopping.,b:You have the right-of-way and can proceed.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,d:You should speed across quickly.
note: Make sure there is room on the far side of the tracks so you won't stop on them. Never pass other vehicles as you approach or cross.

question: When might you drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:In snow or when road/visibility conditions make the posted speed unsafe,b:Only on winding roads,c:Only in heavy traffic
note: Adjust speed to conditions like weather, visibility, road surface, and traffic — even if below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you not omit when changing lanes?
options: a:Check side and rearview mirrors.,b:Use a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers also moving into the same lane.,d:Ignore blind spots and rely on mirrors only.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots, use your signal, and ensure other drivers are not entering the same lane.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how alcohol affects reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Yes, beer affects you less than wine.,b:No, the type does not change the impairment—only the amount consumed.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks always have greater effects.,d:Wine affects reflexes less than liquor.
note: All alcoholic beverages impair reflexes and judgment depending on the amount consumed; the beverage type does not alter the physiological impairment.

question: True or false: Orange signs are used to warn drivers in construction work zones.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only at night,d:Only on highways
note: Most work zone warning signs are orange and diamond-shaped (sometimes rectangular) and are often reflective for visibility.

question: A flashing red traffic signal requires the same action as:
options: a:Stopping at a stop sign,b:Slowing as at a yield sign,c:Continuing through without stopping
note: A flashing red signal requires a complete stop and yielding to traffic the same as a stop sign.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure before changing lanes on a multilane highway?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors and blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Sound your horn before changing lanes.,c:Reduce your speed before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes you should signal, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot; change lanes only when safe.

question: If involved in an accident, what actions should a driver take?
options: a:Stop their vehicle at or near the scene.,b:Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,c:Turn off the ignitions of wrecked vehicles.,d:All of the above.
note: If in a crash, stop at the scene, move vehicles out of traffic if possible, avoid standing in travel lanes, and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles.

question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases under which condition?
options: a:On wet or icy roads,b:On dry paved highways,c:During daylight only
note: Wet, icy, or loose gravel surfaces increase stopping distances and require greater following gaps.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights or siren and approaches, what must a driver do immediately?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Speed up and stay in lane.,c:Ignore and continue driving normally.,d:Pull to the left and stop.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using warning devices, drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' sign means:
options: a:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:That the new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next speed limit sign.,c:That you have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
note: The posted reduced speed limit takes effect at the sign; begin slowing immediately as indicated.

question: What is the act of turning your head to check the blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:A bad driving habit.,b:An unnecessary action.,c:A good driving habit.,d:A mirror-only check.
note: Before changing lanes, glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots is a good habit; do not rely only on mirrors.

question: When may you cross a dashed white line on the highway?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:At any time without checking for traffic.,d:Only to make a U-turn.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; you may cross them to change lanes or pass when it is safe.

question: What should drivers know about large trucks?
options: a:They have large blind spots and need more space to maneuver and stop.,b:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:They require less room to make turns.,d:They always maintain lower speeds than cars.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and need greater room to maneuver and stop. Avoid lingering beside or near them.

question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Drive carefully without stopping.,b:Slow down but do not stop.,c:Stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.,d:Merge to the right and continue.
note: A flashing red signal has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and proceed only when the way is clear, just like a stop sign.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately and honk.,b:Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.,c:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, move to a safe area, and stop.,d:Accelerate to reach the shoulder quickly.
note: When power steering fails, steering becomes heavier. Reduce speed, steer carefully to a safe location, and stop to restore control.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect cars with good tires.
note: Higher speeds reduce tire ability to clear water; excessive speed can cause hydroplaning and loss of control.

question: In fog, should you use high beam headlights to improve vision?
options: a:False,b:True
note: High beams reflect off fog and worsen visibility; use low beams or fog lights and reduce speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Stop before entering from a driveway, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light will appear next?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing red.
note: A steady yellow light signals that the light will soon turn steady red; prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When anything makes conditions less than perfect, such as poor visibility or slippery roads.,b:Only if police direct you to.,c:Only when entering a highway.,d:Never; posted limits are always safe.
note: Reduce speed below the posted limit when road, weather, or visibility conditions make driving unsafe.

question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway,b:Pull out quickly to merge with traffic,c:Stop with part of your car on the roadway to warn others
note: Yield to pedestrians and drivers on the main road when entering from a private road or driveway; merge only when safe.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.,b:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,c:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
note: Be prepared to yield to trains at crossings, especially when no warning devices are active, and ensure there's room to clear the tracks.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what is the recommended technique?
options: a:Firmly pump your brakes.,b:Lightly tap the brakes.,c:Hold down the brake pedal.
note: For vehicles without ABS, pump the brakes firmly and quickly to help the vehicle stop while maintaining the ability to steer.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.,b:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,c:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
note: Always ensure all passengers use seat belts or appropriate child restraints; children 12 and under should ride in the rear seat, and never place a rear-facing infant restraint in front of an active airbag.

question: If a transit bus is signaling to re-enter traffic after stopping, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the bus driver.,b:Yield by changing lanes or slowing to let the bus merge.,c:Speed up to pass the bus.,d:Ignore the signal and continue.
note: Yield to transit vehicles signaling to re-enter traffic after loading or unloading passengers. Change lanes or slow to let them merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center lane reserved for left turns, what maneuvers are generally permitted?
options: a:Making left turns from either direction.,b:Using the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,c:Making U-turns at any time.,d:Driving through without turning.
note: Center turn lanes are generally reserved for left turns from either direction and should not be used for passing or through travel.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving,b:Excessive speed under the driving conditions,c:Following other vehicles too closely,d:All of the above
note: Inattentive driving, excessive speed for conditions, and tailgating are common causes of crashes; all increase risk.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to which condition?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of anger.,d:The effects of cold medication.
note: Fatigue impairs driving like alcohol. Being awake 18 hours can impair driving similar to a BAC of about 0.05% and 24 hours similar to about 0.10%.

question: When a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, how must you respond?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Copy surrounding drivers and ignore the guard.,c:Assume the guard lacks authority and continue.,d:Accelerate through the zone to clear it quickly.
note: Crossing guards direct traffic in school zones; you must follow their instructions and exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
note: A solid yellow indicates the signal is about to turn red; stop before entering if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed through carefully.

question: Why is it important to be especially alert to motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and more easily hidden in blind spots; it's harder to judge their speed and distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does the term 'yield' include stopping if you cannot safely merge into traffic?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: If you must yield to traffic and cannot merge safely, you are expected to stop until it is safe to merge.

question: What is the leading cause of traffic accidents in Nevada?
options: a:Speeding.,b:Failure to yield the right-of-way.,c:Tailgating.
note: Failure to yield the right-of-way is a leading cause of crashes; know and follow right-of-way rules to prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection where a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a signal, who must yield?
options: a:The pedestrian.,b:The driver turning must yield.,c:Whoever started moving last.,d:The faster party.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing intersections without signals, whether or not a crosswalk is marked.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.,b:Go to the next exit.,c:Make a U-turn through the median.
note: If you miss an exit, proceed to the next exit; do not stop, back up, or cross the median on the freeway.

question: Should drivers keep a safe operating distance when near a cyclist?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must maintain a safe distance from cyclists to avoid collisions and account for their unpredictability.

question: What is the effect of consuming alcohol while taking drugs?
options: a:It can increase the effects of both substances and further impair driving.,b:It reduces the effects of alcohol.,c:It cures the illness the drug treats.,d:It has no added risk beyond alcohol alone.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can amplify impairment and greatly increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While driving uphill approaching a heavy truck, what should you be aware of?
options: a:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.,b:You can always safely pass the truck on the hill.,c:The truck will speed up to maintain pace.,d:You may legally pass at any time on the hill.
note: Large trucks often travel slower uphill; on hills with limited visibility, passing can be unsafe or unlawful.

question: Which is NOT a factor in the distance required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance is determined by perception, reaction, and braking distances. Steering ability does not directly determine stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Signal and slow, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound their horn to warn others.,c:Swing right within their lane before the turn.,d:Accelerate to clear the turn quickly.
note: Signal in advance, slow gradually while checking mirrors, move into the left lane when appropriate, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.,c:Stop and then proceed when clear even if the arrow is red.,d:Yield only to pedestrians then go.
note: A red arrow means stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow unless directed otherwise by signs or an officer.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beams (and fog lights if equipped) in fog because high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: If traffic signals are out due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop, yielding appropriately,b:Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping,c:Park and wait for power to be restored
note: When signals are out, drivers should yield as at a four-way stop: stop, determine order, and proceed with caution when safe.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop and wait for a green light,c:Pass through at normal speed
note: A flashing yellow signal warns you to be cautious; slow down, look, and proceed carefully.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Slow down as you approach.
note: Slow down when approaching a roundabout and yield to traffic already in the circle; roundabouts are designed for low-speed operation.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:Railroad crossings.,c:School zones.,d:Stop ahead.
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate you must yield to trains. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods without active scanning.,d:Listening to loud music.
note: Highway hypnosis results from staring straight ahead for long periods and failing to actively scan, which can cause you to zone out and increase crash risk.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving at the same speed.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, steer to keep control, release the accelerator, and slow gradually. Apply the brakes lightly only when the vehicle is under control, then pull off the road.

question: If your wheels slip off the pavement edge, what is the safest recovery method?
options: a:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,b:Grip the wheel, slow gradually, then steer back onto the pavement when safe.,c:Slam on your brakes and stop.
note: Keep control by slowing gently while driving with wheels off the pavement; when at a safe speed, steer smoothly back onto the roadway.

question: Is failure to yield the right-of-way a leading cause of accidents in Nevada?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Failure to yield disrupts traffic flow and is a leading cause of crashes; obey right-of-way rules for safety.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It improves focus and reaction.,b:It lowers your ability to concentrate on driving.,c:It makes you less likely to have an accident.,d:It has no effect on driving ability.
note: Emotions like stress, anger, or sadness can reduce concentration and impair driving. If emotionally unstable, delay driving until calm.

question: A curb painted which color designates a reserved handicap parking space?
options: a:Blue,b:White,c:Yellow
note: Painted curbs show parking restrictions; blue curbs mark spaces reserved for vehicles displaying the proper plate or placard.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke affect driving?
options: a:Are distracting activities.,b:Do not affect driving abilities.,c:Help maintain driver alertness.
note: Smoking while driving can distract you by taking your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already within an intersection and the light turns yellow, what is the correct action?
options: a:You should continue carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Back up to avoid entering the intersection.,d:Signal and turn around.
note: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, proceed through carefully. Do not enter on a yellow light if you can safely stop before the intersection.

question: For drivers 21 and older, what minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes it illegal to drive?
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.,d:0.10 percent.
note: In Nevada, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or greater.

question: What is a safe technique for driving through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter and accelerate as you exit.,b:Maintain the same speed through the entire curve.,c:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.
note: Slow before you enter a curve, maintain a steady path through it, and then gradually accelerate as you exit to regain speed safely.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Do not enter the street or crosswalk if vehicles are approaching,b:Always insist you have the right-of-way over vehicles,c:Enter any time because drivers must stop
note: Pedestrians should avoid entering crosswalks or roadways when vehicles are approaching, since drivers may not have time to stop safely.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase your following distance,b:Speed up to get off the road quickly,c:Ignore it and maintain normal distance
note: In wintry conditions keep your windows and mirrors clear and increase following distance because stopping distances grow on slippery surfaces.

question: How should you behave at a school crossing sign?
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: Be alert for children near crossings and be prepared to stop; yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, look and be ready to stop,b:Stop immediately in all cases,c:Drive faster to clear the tracks quickly
note: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look for trains, and be prepared to stop. If lights flash or gates are down, stop 15–50 feet from the tracks.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Before changing lanes or turning and when pulling toward or away from a curb,b:Only when parallel parking,c:Only when reversing
note: Check blind spots by glancing over your shoulder whenever changing lanes, turning, or pulling to/from a curb.

question: Before starting the ignition, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Buckle your seat belt and ensure all passengers are buckled.,b:Buckle only the adult passengers.,c:Ensure only children are buckled first.,d:Start the car then buckle everyone as you drive.
note: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt before switching on the ignition and ensure every passenger is properly restrained.

question: Are drivers required to stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:True: Yes, drivers must stop.,b:False: Drivers may pass carefully.,c:Only on two-lane roads.,d:Only if children are visible.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the lights are turned off, except in certain divided-roadway situations.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Overcorrect with sharp steering.,b:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid and remain calm.,c:Turn into oncoming traffic.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If a vehicle skids, steer in the direction of the skid to regain control and avoid overcorrecting.

question: What are the driving risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Can make turning more difficult.,b:Are likely to hydroplane.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.
note: Worn tires reduce traction, increasing stopping distance and the risk of hydroplaning and loss of vehicle control.

question: How serious is drinking alcohol and then driving?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving under the influence is a serious safety hazard that impairs your ability to drive and endangers others.

question: Is it ever appropriate to drive as slowly as 10 mph?
options: a:True — some conditions may require driving as slowly as 10 mph,b:False — 10 mph is always too slow,c:Only in school zones
note: Drivers must reduce speed below posted limits when conditions demand, potentially as slow as 10 mph in hazardous situations.

question: On a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross these lines to pass other vehicles, but only if there is no oncoming traffic.,c:Cross these lines under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross them to make left turns into driveways or private roads when safe.

question: Approaching a steady green traffic light, what should drivers do?
options: a:Proceed but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection,b:Stop regardless of the traffic,c:Treat it as a four-way stop
note: A steady green allows you to go, but you must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and vehicles still in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When using a roundabout, what should you do before entering?
options: a:Drive in a clockwise direction.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
note: Roundabouts are driven counterclockwise; you must yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout before entering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing other vehicles is prohibited in which locations?
options: a:At intersections, on hills, curves, and railroad crossings.,b:Only when police are present.,c:Only on one-way streets.,d:Only at night.
note: Passing is unsafe and often illegal at intersections, hills, curves, and railroad crossings, among other places.

question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle. What should you do?
options: a:Flash your headlights to warn the pedestrian.,b:Slow down and be ready to stop, yielding to the pedestrian.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.,d:Honk and proceed if the pedestrian hesitates.
note: Always slow and be prepared to stop for pedestrians, especially in crosswalks. Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing the road.

question: Where is a motorcycle operator allowed to use a full traffic lane?
options: a:On any highway or street where motorcycles are permitted,b:Only on rural highways,c:Only on city streets
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to the full width of a traffic lane wherever motorcycles are allowed; they may ride two abreast in a lane where allowed.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When following a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:Only in city traffic.,c:Only when exiting an expressway.,d:Never, keep a constant distance.
note: Increase following distance when a large vehicle blocks your view, in poor weather, heavy traffic, or when being tailgated.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the outside rearview mirror.,b:Using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: The proper way to check blind spots is to turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is nearby, what must you do?
options: a:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel (pull over if safe),b:Speed up to avoid it,c:Stop in the lane where you are and block it
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens by pulling to the side and stopping when it is safe to allow them to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:Close to the right side of the street.
note: To make a right turn safely, move as far to the right as practicable without crossing curbs or bike lanes.

question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?
options: a:You must stop and then proceed when the light turns circular green.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular green, but you must turn in the arrow's direction.,c:It applies only on one-way streets.,d:It allows any direction of travel from the lane.
note: A green arrow means traffic in the indicated lane may proceed, and drivers must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following takes precedence over the others?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A police officer directing traffic.,c:A stop sign.,d:A flashing yellow light.
note: Directions from authorized traffic officers override signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: Before changing lanes, what sequence should you perform?
options: a:Quickly turn your head to check for other vehicles.,b:Check your side view mirror.,c:Check your rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes check mirrors for approaching traffic and then quickly glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and blinds you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,b:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.,c:Look toward the right side of the road until the car passes.
note: Avoid looking directly at oncoming high beams; look toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
note: Large vehicles require longer stopping distances; other road users should avoid blind spots and give them extra room.

question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?
options: a:Turn your radio down so you can hear an approaching train.,b:Approach cautiously and cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction.,c:Wait for a flagger to tell you when to cross.,d:Stop at least 50 feet from the tracks and open your door to listen.
note: Always approach railroad crossings without active warnings with extreme caution. Cross only when you are certain no train is approaching from any direction. Obey a flagger if one is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Signal only if traffic is present, then change lanes.,c:Check the blind spot only if you hear a horn.,d:Turn your head quickly without signaling.
note: Always signal in advance, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to on the road?
options: a:Half the width of a lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:The bicycle lane only.,d:Only the right edge of the lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as other motor vehicles and should be afforded full-lane space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, look both ways, and watch for pedestrians and other traffic.

question: When driving in fog, should you use your low-beam headlights?
options: a:TRUE: Use low-beam headlights in fog.,b:FALSE: Use high beams in fog.,c:Use parking lights only.,d:Use four-way flashers instead.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog because high beams reflect off fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to use a shared center turn lane?
options: a:As a travel lane to pass other vehicles.,b:To make a left turn onto another street, road, or driveway.,c:To make a right turn onto another street or highway.
note: A shared center turn lane is for making left turns onto or from a roadway or driveway only. It is not a through or passing lane.

question: If a train is near enough to be dangerous, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,c:Cross the tracks at your own risk.
note: Do not cross railroad tracks if a train is close enough to be a hazard; wait until it has fully passed and signals have ceased.

question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Slow down to provide space in front of your vehicle for them to pass safely.,c:Maintain exact speed so they cannot pass.,d:Change lanes immediately regardless of traffic.
note: Slow slightly to create space in front of your vehicle, allowing the passing driver to return to the lane safely.

question: Is nighttime the safest time for cyclists to ride?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Cyclists are harder to see at night even with lights and reflectors; both drivers and cyclists must exercise extra caution.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:Less dangerous.,b:No different.,c:More dangerous.,d:Only more dangerous on rural roads.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous because visibility is reduced, glare is more problematic, and there may be more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road.

question: What should you do first when your visibility is reduced?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Turn on your windshield wipers.
note: Your first reaction to decreased visibility should be to slow down. Use headlights and wipers as needed, but reducing speed improves safety immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Stop completely and proceed when safe.,b:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Continue driving, as you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red light is to be treated like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: When a curb is painted red, what does it generally indicate?
options: a:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time.,b:Drivers may park for a limited time.,c:Only handicap parking is allowed.,d:Loading zones only.
note: Painted curbs convey parking rules; red curbs generally mean no stopping, standing, or parking at any time.

question: When backing, what is the proper technique?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while backing.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open your door while reversing.,d:Back quickly to minimize time spent reversing.
note: When backing, turn and look through the rear window; do not depend solely on mirrors or sensors, especially where children may be present.

question: What is one primary effect of alcohol on driving ability?
options: a:Puts you to sleep.,b:Wakes you up.,c:Slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity, reducing reaction time and impairing judgment needed for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A speed limit sign.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when safe — just like a stop sign.

question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane,b:When it requires driving off the pavement,c:On a narrow bridge
note: You may pass on the right when a vehicle ahead is turning left and a safe lane to the right is available; never pass by leaving the roadway.

question: What can happen to a bicyclist who doesn't obey traffic laws?
options: a:Is in the right because bicyclists don’t have to obey traffic laws.,b:Can be ticketed.,c:Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as motorists and can be cited for violations of traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a stop is required at an intersection but no stop line or crosswalk is marked, what should a driver do?
options: a:Is not required to stop.,b:Slow down to make sure crossing traffic is clear.,c:Stop only where you can see at least 200 feet in each direction, even if you must enter the intersection.
note: If no stop line or crosswalk is present, stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the roadway. Do not move into the intersection to improve your view.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Only if you are in a hurry.,b:When the train has fully passed and gates are raised.,c:Under no circumstances.,d:If the lights have stopped flashing but gates are still down.
note: Never go around a lowered gate. Stop and wait until warning devices stop and the gates are fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against a red signal. What should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.,b:Honk your horn.,c:Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
note: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection to avoid causing a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to exceed the speed limit while passing another vehicle?
options: a:Yes, if you pass quickly.,b:No, exceeding the posted speed limit is always unlawful.,c:Only on multi-lane highways.,d:Only during daylight hours.
note: It is illegal to exceed posted speed limits even when passing another vehicle.

question: How can you avoid a truck or bus blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your lights at them.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots to the sides and rear; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate.

question: When a curb is painted green, what does it normally indicate?
options: a:Drivers may park for a limited time.,b:No stopping at any time.,c:Handicapped parking only.,d:Loading and unloading only.
note: Green curbs usually allow parking for a limited amount of time, often as specified by nearby signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously, who yields?
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.,b:Passing is not allowed.,c:Passing is allowed if you are at the top a hill.
note: Two solid yellow lines down the center mean no passing from either direction, except to turn into a driveway or as otherwise allowed by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, you arrive simultaneously with a vehicle on your right. Who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You, because you were following traffic signs.,b:The vehicle on your right.,c:Whoever signals first.,d:You if you are turning left.
note: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the proper action?
options: a:Use any speed and merge quickly.,b:Signal, accelerate to match traffic speed, and merge into a gap.,c:Stop at the ramp end and wait for a large gap.,d:Merge slowly below highway speed to be cautious.
note: Use acceleration lanes to reach highway speed, signal, look for an opening, and merge safely into traffic.

question: What is the best response to a tailgater?
options: a:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: To reduce the risk of rear-end collisions, change lanes if safe or gradually slow to allow the tailgater to pass.

question: Which action most reduces the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure.,b:Do not speed when the roads are wet.,c:Replace tires with bad tread.
note: Hydroplaning risk increases with speed and with tires that have low pressure or worn tread; reducing speed on wet roads helps prevent it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two drivers arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: When two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on your right.

question: When a traffic signal displays a flashing yellow arrow for left turns, what may drivers do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before turning.,b:Merge immediately without yielding.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow permits left turns, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane road with a 'Merging traffic' sign, what is the appropriate response?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles; move over if no one is beside you.,b:Always remain at your current speed regardless of merging traffic.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.,d:Speed up to prevent merging vehicles from entering.
note: When lanes merge, give space to entering vehicles by changing lanes if it is safe to do so and no vehicle is beside you.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the immediate correct action?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull up the pedal.,b:Shift into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake while keeping eyes on the road.,c:Shift to park to stop the engine.,d:Turn off the ignition while driving fast.
note: If the accelerator sticks, stay focused on the road, shift into neutral, apply steady braking, pull off traffic, and then turn off the engine.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey a specified instruction are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs,b:Information signs,c:Warning signs
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do in that area (speed limits, no turns, etc.).

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Octagon (eight-sided).,b:Rectangle.,c:Circle.,d:Triangle.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is used exclusively for stop signs and means you must come to a complete stop.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the train.,b:Stop if a train is nearby and never go around lowered gates.,c:Look for a detour to bypass the crossing.,d:Cross quickly without slowing.
note: Railroad crossing warnings mean trains may be present; be prepared to stop and never go around lowered gates or ignore warnings.

question: When driving in fog, should you use high beams?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not use high beams in fog; low beams or fog lights reduce glare and improve visibility.

question: Does increasing your speed increase your stopping distance?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Higher speeds increase the distance needed to perceive, react, and stop, so stopping distance grows as speed increases.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.,d:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only effective method for the body to reduce BAC; other measures do not lower your blood alcohol level.

question: How should you position your vehicle relative to a motorcycle on the road?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are full-size roadway users and must be given a full lane; never share a lane with a motorcycle.

question: If you are stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting for the officer to approach?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
note: Remain in the vehicle, keep hands visible on the wheel, and wait for the officer's instructions before retrieving documents.

question: Are you allowed to text while driving?
options: a:If they are very skilled drivers.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:At any time in any manner.
note: Using a handheld device to send or read non-voice communications (including texting) while driving is prohibited.

question: If the driver ahead is distracted (one hand on wheel, talking), what should you do?
options: a:Avoid following the driver's example.,b:Give the vehicle extra space.,c:Know that the driver in the vehicle ahead is reducing their safety margin by being an inattentive driver.
note: If a nearby driver appears distracted, increase the gap between your vehicles to reduce the risk of collision.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Weaving between lanes.,b:Driving exactly at the speed limit.,c:Always using turn signals.,d:Parking perfectly in marked spots.
note: Weaving, erratic speed changes, and sudden stops are common indicators of impaired driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your plans.,b:Just after you start to pass.,c:Only if asked by other drivers.,d:Never; passing requires no signal.
note: Signal in enough time before passing so other drivers are aware of your intention to change lanes or pass.

question: If you see or hear an emergency vehicle while on a divided multilane highway, how should you respond?
options: a:Disregard the signal if there are other lanes available for the emergency vehicle.,b:Slow down, move your vehicle to provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle, and stop.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: Provide a clear path for the emergency vehicle by slowing and moving over; do not attempt to outrun or block it.

question: At night when another vehicle is approaching, what headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Low beams.,c:Parking lights only.,d:No lights if the street is lit.
note: Use low-beam headlights when approaching or following other vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to which sign?
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Yield sign.,c:Stop sign.,d:School zone sign.
note: A red flashing light has the same meaning as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe.

question: If you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: You must immediately yield right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping until the emergency vehicle passes.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim its high beams, where should you look?
options: a:The center of the road.,b:Either side of the road at random.,c:The right side of the road.,d:Directly into the bright lights to gauge intensity.
note: When faced with high beams, glance toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded and maintain your lane position until the vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Has the right-of-way.,c:May force their way into traffic.
note: Vehicles entering the interstate must yield to traffic already traveling on the highway and merge safely when there is space.

question: How close to a railroad crossing may you legally park?
options: a:100 feet,b:75 feet,c:50 feet
note: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing so approaching trains and drivers can see clearly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, which scan pattern should you use before moving forward?
options: a:Look right first, then left, then right again.,b:Check only the vehicle ahead then go.,c:Look left only because those vehicles are closer.,d:Look in the mirrors and proceed immediately.
note: At intersections, look right-left-right to ensure no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching before proceeding after a stop.

question: When driving in an area where children may be present, what should you expect?
options: a:To know when it is safe to cross the street.,b:To stop at the curb before crossing the street.,c:They may run out in front of you without looking.
note: Children may act unpredictably and run into the street; slow down and be prepared to stop.

question: Which of these will help reverse the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Time.,c:Fresh air.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize alcohol; coffee or fresh air do not speed recovery from impairment.

question: While driving on major highways, you should:
options: a:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be ready to react to hazards,b:Stare straight ahead to avoid distraction,c:Relax and let cruise control handle everything
note: To avoid 'highway hypnosis' remain alert, scan frequently, and be prepared to respond to unexpected hazards.

question: What is a vehicle's blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:What you see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that can't be seen in mirrors. Check them by glancing over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: Orange work zone signs indicate:
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions and construction activity ahead,b:The start of a school zone,c:A hospital nearby
note: Work zones use orange signs to warn drivers of roadwork and changed conditions; slow down and follow directions.

question: May you use only parking lights while driving at night?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is unlawful to drive at night using only parking lights; headlights are required when visibility is reduced at night.

question: True or false: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated like a yield sign.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only at night,d:Only with lights flashing
note: A crossbuck means yield: slow down, look for trains, and yield the right-of-way to trains and railroad equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:Only to make a turn into a driveway or side road.,b:At any time for passing.,c:During daylight hours only.,d:When following a large vehicle.
note: Solid yellow lines generally should not be crossed except when making permitted turns into driveways or side roads when safe.

question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open, what is the safest procedure?
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Turn off the ignition, apply brakes carefully, and steer to a safe area.
note: If the throttle sticks, turn off the ignition carefully to stop the engine (without locking steering), apply brakes, and move off the road.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked on the side of the road, what should you assume?
options: a:Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.,b:Speed up.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: Expect occupants to open doors or step out; give extra space and pass cautiously.

question: When approaching an unprotected railroad crossing without signals, what should you do?
options: a:Always come to a full stop regardless of visibility.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is near.,c:Assume there is always a signal at every crossing.,d:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.
note: At crossings without active warnings, slow and be ready to stop. Look and listen for trains before proceeding. Obey flaggers if present.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if the bus is stopped on the shoulder and empty.,b:If the bus is stopped with red lights flashing to load or unload children.,c:Only if students are in the roadway.,d:Never if you are in the opposing lane.
note: On two-lane highways, you must stop and remain stopped when a school bus displays flashing red lights and is loading or unloading children.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII charges?
options: a:Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and some prescription/OTC medicines,b:Only beer and wine,c:Only illegal drugs
note: A wide variety of intoxicants — alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over-the-counter medicines — can impair driving.

question: When is it illegal to drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:When your slow driving disrupts the normal flow of traffic,b:Whenever you are in a construction zone,c:Only on rural roads
note: Driving so slowly that you impede normal traffic flow is illegal and unsafe; adjust speed to conditions without obstructing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Vehicles in the roundabout.,b:Bicyclists in the roundabout.,c:Pedestrians in the roundabout.,d:All of the above.
note: When entering a roundabout you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already circulating in the roundabout.
