question: What color are regulatory signs typically?
options: a:White,b:Blue,c:Green
note: Regulatory signs are usually white with black or red markings and convey laws or regulations that must be obeyed by motorists.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.,b:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,c:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,d:All of the above
note: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving: slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you that may not slow.

question: At a light rail crossing, drivers should always:
options: a:Look both ways before crossing and obey all signals and signs,b:Assume the train will stop for you,c:Drive around lowered gates if there's no train in sight
note: Never drive around lowered gates. Always look both ways before turning across tracks and obey crossing signals and signs.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and turn the front wheels away from the curb so a rolling vehicle will roll into the curb.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination could multiply the effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.,c:The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
note: Alcohol mixed with medications can multiply impairing effects and increase danger; some combinations can be unpredictable and serious.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The largest vehicle.,b:The car on the left.,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: True or False: It is safe to use cruise control when driving on snowy or icy roads as long as you reduce speed.
options: a:True,b:False
note: False. Do not use cruise control on snowy or icy roads because it can reduce your ability to react and regain traction.

question: When must you pull to the edge of the road and allow an emergency vehicle to pass?
options: a:Regardless of your direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights no matter its direction of approach.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Black
note: Yellow lines are used to separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When encountering a flashing red light at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed if clear.,b:Treat it as a stop sign and come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Ignore it if there is no traffic.,d:Only yield to vehicles on your left.
note: A flashing red light means stop, look both ways, and proceed only when it is safe—same as a stop sign.

question: What should a driver do if taking a non-prescription drug?
options: a:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Read the labels on the drug before driving.
note: Many over-the-counter medicines can impair driving; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the stopped vehicle.,b:Stay in your lane and maintain your speed.,c:Drive to the right and stop immediately.
note: If an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, change lanes away from it if it is safe. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the posted limit and give as much space as possible.

question: You begin driving as it starts to rain. What should you do?
options: a:Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down.
note: Reduce speed when rain begins, use headlights, and pull off if visibility is too poor to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn on city streets should you signal?
options: a:20 feet,b:50 feet,c:100 feet
note: On city streets, signal at least 100 feet before turning to alert other drivers and pedestrians of your intention.

question: Which of the following is a correct rule about passing other vehicles?
options: a:You may not pass on a hill or in a curve.,b:You may pass another vehicle by using the shoulder of the highway.,c:Passing is allowed if your lane is next to a solid yellow line.
note: Never attempt to pass on hills or curves where you cannot see oncoming traffic; do not use the shoulder or cross solid yellow lines to pass.

question: How should you treat railroad crossings?
options: a:Dangerous.,b:Safe to cross since a train is unlikely.,c:Safe places to park a car.
note: Railroad crossings should always be treated as hazardous. Look and listen for trains from both directions and obey signs, signals, and flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe to do so.

question: Should drivers avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large vehicles have substantial blind spots; avoid staying beside them for long—either fall back or move ahead to remain visible to the truck driver.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glancing toward the right edge of the roadway helps avoid being blinded by another driver's high beams.

question: If driving at 40 mph or slower, what is the minimum recommended following distance?
options: a:Two seconds,b:Three seconds,c:Four seconds
note: At speeds of 40 mph or less, a minimum two-second following distance is recommended; increase distance in poor conditions.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light instructs drivers to:
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for green.,c:Yield only to pedestrians.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for hazards.

question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Use the lane of oncoming traffic (i.e., cross the centerline) only when safe and legal,b:Never cross the centerline,c:Flash your headlights as the only signal
note: Passing on a two-lane road requires entering the oncoming traffic lane; only do so when you have sufficient sight distance and it is legal to pass.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open your window.,b:Stop driving.,c:Get some coffee.
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous; the best remedy is to stop driving and rest.

question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery roads you should increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead because stopping will take longer.

question: Is it legal to park in a handicap access aisle beside a handicap parking stall?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Handicap access aisles must remain clear to allow wheelchair access and lifts; parking there is prohibited.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly increase crash risk?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction that raises the likelihood of a crash and is unsafe.

question: When may you sound your horn?
options: a:To warn others when you have lost control of your car or to avoid collisions,b:To express frustration at slow drivers,c:When approaching every intersection
note: Use the horn to warn of imminent danger or loss of vehicle control; do not use it to express anger or impatience.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver to arrive first has the right-of-way.,b:The driver to arrive last has the right-of-way.,c:One driver should continue driving without stopping.
note: At four-way stops, the vehicle that arrives first should proceed first; if two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: After being stopped by law enforcement, should a driver immediately exit the vehicle and approach the officer?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible unless the officer asks you to exit; this improves safety for everyone involved.

question: If waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while waiting to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if struck from behind,b:Keep wheels turned left so you can complete the turn faster,c:Flash your headlights so others will let you through
note: Signal for your turn and keep the front wheels straight while waiting; if rear-ended you won't be pushed into oncoming lanes.

question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:
options: a:You can see clearly ahead and can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives,b:There is a shoulder to use for passing,c:You have the other vehicle's permission
note: To pass safely you must have adequate sight distance, be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and be capable of the needed speed.

question: Which factors influence the effects of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:The body weight of an individual,c:How much time passes between drinks.,d:All of the above.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration depends on how much you drink, how quickly, your weight, and whether you've eaten; all these influence impairment.

question: Compared to smaller vehicles, larger vehicles typically have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:Larger blind spots.,c:No blind spots.,d:Blind spots only in front.
note: Larger vehicles such as trucks and buses have bigger blind spots; be mindful when driving near them.

question: When there's an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Split the difference.,b:Let the car pass and then pass the bicyclist.,c:Pull onto the shoulder.
note: Avoid trying to deal with two hazards at once: let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.
note: Do not make last-minute lane changes or turns; proceed to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

question: If someone is injured in an accident you caused, what should you do regarding the injured person?
options: a:Move the injured person immediately away from the scene regardless of injuries.,b:Leave the injured exactly where they are and do not render assistance.,c:Avoid moving the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and provide first aid if trained.,d:Wait for others to move them before offering aid.
note: Do not move injured persons unless necessary. Keep them warm and administer first aid only if you are trained; moving them improperly can worsen injuries.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?
options: a:Only if you are not driving.,b:Never while on a public road.,c:If riding in the back of a pickup truck.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess an open alcoholic beverage while on a public road; open containers in areas accessible to driver or passengers are prohibited.

question: What does a single dashed white line separating lanes indicate?
options: a:Drivers may change lanes or pass when safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes traveling the same direction; you may change lanes or pass when it is safe to do so.

question: If the solid white edge line on the right slopes leftward, what does it indicate?
options: a:The road ahead becomes narrower.,b:There is an intersection ahead.,c:A construction area is ahead.,d:You are required to turn left shortly.
note: An edge line angling toward the center means the road narrows ahead; watch for changes in lane width.

question: When should you use your parking brake?
options: a:Every time you park.,b:Only when parking on an incline.,c:Only when parked in a driveway.
note: Whenever you park, turn off the engine and set the parking brake. Do not rely on the transmission alone to hold the vehicle in place.

question: When confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Retaliate by tailgating them.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
note: Do not engage with aggressive drivers; try to put distance between you and them, avoid eye contact, and let them go on.

question: Why is driving at night generally more difficult than during the day?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,c:It is always raining at night.,d:Traffic laws are different at night.
note: At night your field of vision is reduced; use proper headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within visible distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is walking against the traffic light?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if a pedestrian misjudges a traffic signal and walks against the light.

question: What color lines divide lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Red.,d:Blue.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: Does drinking coffee reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes, it decreases BAC.,b:No, it has no effect on BAC.,c:It cancels the effects of alcohol.,d:It dilutes alcohol in the bloodstream.
note: Coffee does not reduce BAC or sober you up. Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with siren, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.,c:Turn into the middle lane.
note: When turning onto a multilane street moving in your direction, enter the lane nearest to the lane you came from and do not change lanes while completing the turn.

question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and may turn right if not prohibited and the way is clear,b:Proceed through if no other cars are present,c:Ignore it when no police officer is present
note: A steady red requires a full stop; a right turn on red is allowed unless posted otherwise and if safe to do so.

question: Are cell phones a serious source of driver distraction?
options: a:FALSE,b:TRUE
note: Cell phones and other electronic devices can significantly distract drivers and should be used only for emergencies while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light changes from green to yellow as you approach, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Apply the brakes sharply to stop.,c:Be prepared to stop.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; slow and prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,b:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and minds or the vehicles being driven.,c:Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time; intoxicated drivers lack adequate control.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite directions and indicates passing is allowed when it is safe to do so.

question: Is the speed limit in Nevada school zones always 25 mph?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Nevada school zone limits may be 15 or 25 mph depending on signage; posted times apply unless otherwise indicated.

question: When sharing the road with large commercial vehicles, which should you keep in mind?
options: a:They require extra time and space to slow and stop.,b:They always drive slower than posted speeds.,c:They have small blind spots.,d:They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
note: Large commercial vehicles need extra time and distance to stop; they also have large blind spots. Signal your moves well in advance.

question: What should you do when you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as is safe and stop.,b:Proceed slowly and allow the vehicle to pass.,c:Stop immediately where you are.
note: On a two-lane or undivided highway, safely pull as far right as possible and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass. Do not stop in an intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or false: Your stopping distance after you brake is affected by how fast you were driving.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE,c:Only on wet roads,d:Only when you have good brakes
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; the faster you travel, the farther your vehicle will go after you brake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn into a driveway or make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving vehicle.,c:To pass another car when traffic is clear.,d:Whenever there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing or lane changes. You may cross them only to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make other permitted left turns.

question: True or false: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane, you must yield the right-of-way.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,d:Only if a crossing guard is present
note: Pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes have right-of-way; yield and provide them space to cross safely.

question: When waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection with obstructed view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross and can make the turn safely,b:Accelerate quickly once the first lane clears,c:Start when an oncoming driver waves you through
note: Do not begin a left turn until you have a clear view of all lanes you will cross and can complete the maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway?
options: a:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.,b:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,c:Signal and enter the freeway. Freeway traffic must yield.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway traffic speed, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

question: True or false: A 'Merging lanes' sign means drivers should be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic into their lane.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only merge if on a freeway.,d:Only applies to trucks
note: A 'Merging lanes' sign warns that two lanes will become one and drivers should be ready to yield or change lanes as needed.

question: If a flagger directs traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions,b:Follow only the surrounding traffic's actions,c:Assume the flagger's signs are optional
note: Flaggers are controlling traffic for safety in work zones; obey their instructions and slow down as directed.

question: If you will turn left onto a one-way street, you should turn into which lane?
options: a:The lane closest to your previous lane,b:The right-most lane,c:Either lane at your discretion
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, enter the lane closest to the lane you came from (usually the leftmost lane available).

question: Which statement about passing a motorcycle is true?
options: a:You must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle,b:It is okay to follow a motorcycle closely,c:Motorcycles are always more balanced with two riders
note: Motorcycles are entitled to an entire lane; when passing you must move fully into the adjacent lane to pass safely.

question: What is required when you encounter an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Ignore it and keep driving.,b:Yield the right-of-way and follow any instructions given over loudspeaker.,c:Speed up to pass it quickly.,d:Turn on your hazard lights and maintain your lane.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or lights, moving out of their path and following any loudspeaker instructions. Proceed only when safe.

question: A red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop at the stop line or before entering any crosswalk or intersection,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Ignore it if no other cars are present
note: On red you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, or before entering the intersection until the light changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Back up slowly.
note: A green light allows you to go but you must yield to pedestrians and traffic still in the intersection.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,b:A reflective orange triangle.,c:A rectangular red sign.
note: A slow-moving vehicle is identified by a reflective orange triangle-shaped emblem; such vehicles typically travel 25 mph or less.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning while driving in wet conditions?
options: a:Drive more quickly through shallow water.,b:Drive more slowly and avoid standing water.,c:Increase tire pressure above recommended levels.,d:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning risk increases with speed; reduce speed and avoid standing water to lower the risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line next to your lane means:
options: a:Do not pass from your direction.,b:You may pass with caution.,c:Slow down to below the speed limit.,d:You must change lanes immediately.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited from your direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What sequence should you follow when changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, look over your shoulder to check the blind spot, and then change lanes when it is safe.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops.,b:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.,c:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.
note: Avoid sudden stops and slow gradually so drivers behind have time to react; use smooth braking and signal intent when slowing.

question: What does an 'End school zone' sign indicate?
options: a:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,b:The increased possibility of encountering pedestrians.,c:End of the reduced speed school zone.
note: An 'End school zone' sign marks the end of a reduced-speed school zone and the return to the normal speed limit.

question: True or false: If conditions are unsafe, you may not leave a child under eight unattended in a vehicle.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only on highways,d:Only with windows cracked
note: Never leave a child under eight unattended in a vehicle if conditions pose a significant health or safety risk; a responsible person at least 12 should supervise.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the curb and stop, then look to see if it is on your street,b:Keep driving until you spot it,c:Ignore the sound
note: If you hear an emergency siren and don't know where it is coming from, safely pull over and stop to allow it to pass.

question: Which practice can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time.,b:Only use turn signals when necessary.,c:Drive faster than posted limits.,d:Ignore posted speed limits to keep up with traffic.
note: Allow plenty of travel time, obey posted speed limits, and use proper signals to help reduce road rage incidents.

question: Large trucks' blind spots can extend how far behind the vehicle?
options: a:Up to 200 feet,b:Only a few feet,c:They have no blind spots
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots that may extend up to about 200 feet behind; avoid tailgating and stay visible to the driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you view a driver who travels much slower than the flow of traffic?
options: a:Is always the safest driver.,b:May be hazardous and must allow others to pass if backing up traffic.,c:Should not let following cars pass.
note: Driving significantly slower than traffic can be hazardous; if you are holding up traffic on a two-lane road you must pull off and let others pass.

question: The term 'No zone' refers to:
options: a:The blind spots around a truck or bus where the driver cannot see you,b:A special reduced-speed zone,c:An area where radios must be turned off
note: Large trucks and buses have significant blind spots front, rear, and sides where smaller vehicles disappear from view; these are called No Zones.

question: When there is a stop sign but no crosswalk, where must you stop?
options: a:Before entering the intersection,b:At the stop line if present, otherwise before entering the intersection or crosswalk,c:In the middle of the intersection
note: Stop at the stop line if there is one; if not, stop before a crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure tires have good tread and proper pressure and reduce speed in rain.,b:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.,c:Turn off traction control.,d:Use parking lights only in rain.
note: Maintain proper tire tread and inflation and reduce speed in wet conditions to lower hydroplaning risk, which increases with speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal displays a red light and a green arrow simultaneously, may you turn in the arrow’s direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: True. After yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection, you may turn in the direction indicated by a green arrow even if the circular light is red.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the best response?
options: a:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.,b:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: Remain calm and allow the aggressive driver to go on; do not engage or retaliate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver plans to stop or slow down.,b:The driver plans to turn left.,c:The driver plans to turn right.,d:The driver is signaling for you to pass.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver intends to stop or slow; adjust your driving accordingly.

question: A solid red arrow displayed by a traffic signal means:
options: a:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not turn in the arrow's direction,b:You may turn after yielding to oncoming traffic without stopping,c:It has no legal meaning
note: A solid red arrow carries the same restriction as a circular red: traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the arrow's direction.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only when you see a train.,b:When directed by a flagger, stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,c:Never; always proceed unless a train is visible.,d:Only if the crossing is marked with a crossbuck.
note: Stop at a railroad crossing when instructed by a sign or flagger and whenever flashing red signals or gates indicate an approaching train.

question: True or false: Increasing your speed is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only with four-wheel drive,d:Only on highways
note: Increasing speed increases the risk of hydroplaning. The best defense on wet roads is to reduce speed.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's driving ability?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:A lack of sleep.,c:Any medication.
note: Driving ability can be impaired by alcohol, by many medications (prescription or over-the-counter), and by fatigue.

question: Why must drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are harder to see and less protected than occupants of motor vehicles,b:They obey completely different traffic laws,c:They always have the right-of-way
note: Smaller road users are harder to detect and more vulnerable; drivers should be extra vigilant to avoid collisions.

question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and pay extra attention.,b:Work zones are always stationary and use black and white signs.,c:Work zones do not require drivers to change behavior.,d:Work zones require you to stop at all times.
note: Work zones can be stationary or moving, are marked with orange signs, and require reduced speed and heightened attention.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe ride home?
options: a:Ride with a friend who has not been drinking,b:Drink coffee before driving,c:Take a cold shower before driving
note: Only arranging a sober ride home ensures you are not driving impaired; coffee or cold showers do not lower blood alcohol content.

question: When driving near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, how should you behave?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Take the right-of-way.,c:Proceed normally.
note: Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop for blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog.

question: Where should you maintain space around your vehicle for safety?
options: a:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,b:Only in front of the vehicle.,c:Only in back of your vehicle.,d:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: Maintain a cushion of space on all sides to allow time and room to react to hazards or make evasive maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is the correct time to slow down when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:After you move onto the exit ramp.,b:Before you enter the exit ramp.,c:Keep speed constant until you reach the off-ramp end.,d:Only after exiting the ramp entirely.
note: Do not slow down on the main travel lane; begin reducing speed after moving onto the exit ramp so traffic behind is not affected.

question: What should drivers do when road conditions are bad (rain, snow, fog)?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Increase their speed to reach the destination more quickly.,c:Decrease their following distance.
note: In adverse weather increase the space between you and other vehicles to allow more time to react and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Are drivers always allowed to make U-turns in school zones?
options: a:True: U-turns are always permitted.,b:False: U-turns are restricted in school zones except when allowed.,c:Only allowed during school hours.,d:Only allowed with a police officer present.
note: Nevada restricts U-turns in school zones unless conditions make it safe (no children present, school not in session, or posted allowances).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a red light together with a green arrow, what does it mean?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.,b:You may only drive straight ahead.,c:You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
note: When a green arrow is displayed with a red light, you may proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow and only if the intersection is clear.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your driving?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only prescription drugs.,c:Illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medications.,d:Only alcohol combined with drugs.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving under impairment may be a criminal offense.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a marked bicycle lane or on a crosswalk.,c:In a parking lot.,d:On private property with permission.
note: Do not park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. When street parking, stay within 12 inches of the curb.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: A broken yellow centerline indicates opposing traffic; the road is two-way and passing may be allowed when safe.

question: Which of the following are effects of alcohol?
options: a:Loss of concentration.,b:Poor coordination.,c:Slower judgment.,d:All of the above.
note: Alcohol impairs concentration, coordination, judgment, and other skills essential for safe driving.

question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?
options: a:Always come to a full stop.,b:Yield—slow down and yield the right-of-way, be prepared to stop.,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is present.,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead.
note: A downward-pointing red and white triangle is a yield sign—slow down, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and be prepared to stop.

question: Which describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,b:Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.,c:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is one who is distracted or daydreaming, failing to scan the roadway and check mirrors regularly.

question: Who should wear seat belts for maximum effectiveness?
options: a:Only the driver.,b:All occupants of the vehicle.,c:Only those in the front seats.,d:Only on long drives.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant in the vehicle wears one. Unbelted passengers can become projectiles in a crash.

question: Is it unlawful to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must not drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane; motorcycles require a full lane to maneuver safely.

question: Which is true about drowsy drivers?
options: a:Drinking coffee will reliably keep them alert.,b:Drowsy drivers can appear to be intoxicated and should not rely on windows or radio for alertness.,c:Opening a window solves drowsiness.,d:They always drive slower than traffic.
note: Drowsiness can mimic intoxication and simple measures like coffee or open windows are often insufficient. Rest is required to restore alertness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver signals with the left arm and hand extended upward. What does this signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn left.,d:The driver intends to reverse.
note: A left arm bent upward signals an intended right turn. Recognize hand signals and respond safely.

question: What is the risk of taking drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It lessens the effect of alcohol.,d:It neutralizes both substances.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can significantly increase impairment and crash risk.

question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks even briefly when moving with a stream of vehicles?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never stop on railroad tracks. Make sure there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side before crossing.

question: On an open highway, you should signal how far before a turn?
options: a:At least 300 feet (about 100 feet is insufficient),b:20 feet,c:50 feet
note: On open highways signal at least 300 feet before your turn or lane change; closer distances like 20 or 50 feet are for different contexts.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?
options: a:Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.,b:Stay in your car and wait for help.,c:Get out of the car and go for help.
note: If stranded in severe weather, remain with your vehicle which is easier for rescuers to locate; run the engine only periodically for heat and ensure ventilation.
